item.title: Esquiva a la policía y llega a la manifestación: un juego online se vuelve viral en la India
item.description: Un juego en línea en el que los participantes deben esquivar a la policía y evitar ser detenidos mientras se dirigen al lugar de una manifestación en Nueva Delhi se ha vuelto viral, mientras los jóvenes indios recurren a la sátira y al humor para responder a la represión policial.
item.dc:creator: Tora Agarwala, Aftab Ahmed
item.content:encoded: Un juego en línea en el que los participantes deben esquivar a la policía y evitar ser detenidos mientras se dirigen al lugar de una manifestación en Nueva Delhi se ha vuelto viral, mientras los jóvenes indios recurren a la sátira y al humor para responder a la represión policial. Mientras las protestas lideradas por los jóvenes contra el desempleo, las filtraciones de exámenes y las revisiones del censo electoral se extienden por toda la India, una creciente ola de juegos en línea está transformando las reivindicaciones políticas en contenido digital que se puede compartir. La tendencia pone de manifiesto que una generación que ha crecido con Instagram está expresando su disconformidad de formas que difieren notablemente del estilo de comunicación política del primer ministro Narendra Modi. Uno de estos juegos, "Jantar Mantar Chalo", fue desarrollado por Suraj Kushwah, un profesional de las tecnologías de la información de 27 años, que lo ha descrito como "humor negro". El juego satiriza las dificultades a las que se enfrentan los manifestantes para llegar a Jantar Mantar, uno de los principales puntos de protesta de la capital, en un contexto de bloqueos policiales, cortes de carreteras y suspensiones del transporte público. Los jugadores pueden formar una "kafila" (procesión), eludir los controles y organizar una manifestación, o cambiar de bando y utilizar porras y gas lacrimógeno para dispersar a la multitud. "Las noticias que llegaban eran como un circo", dijo Kushwah. "La gente intentaba llegar a Jantar Mantar. Y acababan siendo detenidos. Y me lo imaginé como un juego en 3D". Kushwah dijo que, en todo momento desde su lanzamiento el 14 de octubre, al menos 2.000 personas habían estado jugando al juego. Otro juego presenta a la activista de izquierdas Neha Bora como protagonista de un juego retro de 8 bits que recuerda a los clásicos de las salas recreativas. "Nosotros, como artistas, creemos que la sátira es la forma más poderosa de hablar de las cosas", dijo Anav Nayar, de 30 años, quien desarrolló el juego junto con su hermano, Akshay. Las protestas se desencadenaron a raíz del movimiento juvenil "cucaracha", que también comenzó como una broma en Internet. Los juegos se inspiran en las protestas contra la revisión del censo electoral llevada a cabo por una comisión, que, según los partidos de la oposición y los activistas, ha privado del derecho al voto a 130 millones de personas y ha favorecido al Partido Bharatiya Janata (BJP) de Modi. La Comisión Electoral y el BJP niegan las acusaciones. El estilo de expresión de la Generación Z plantea un reto inusual para Modi. Después de que el movimiento "cucaracha" obligó a dimitir al ministro de Educación de Modi en julio, este intensificó sus esfuerzos por llegar a los jóvenes indios a través de videos de Instagram grabados por él mismo. Sin embargo, los analistas señalan que el acercamiento de Modi podría no ser suficiente. "El BJP ha disfrutado durante bastante tiempo de su dominio a la hora de controlar el discurso tanto en Internet como sobre el terreno, pero esta vez la generación más joven les ha plantado cara en todas partes", dijo Rasheed Kidwai, analista político.

item.title: Blue Origin vise plusieurs vols de New Glenn par semaine d’ici à 2030
item.description: Blue Origin vise plusieurs vols par semaine de sa fusée New Glenn d’ici à la fin de la décennie, a déclaré vendredi un dirigeant de l’entreprise, alors que celle-ci investit des milliards de dollars dans les infrastructures nécessaires pour rivaliser avec SpaceX .
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Blue Origin vise plusieurs vols par semaine de sa fusée New Glenn d’ici à la fin de la décennie, a déclaré vendredi un dirigeant de l’entreprise, alors que celle-ci investit des milliards de dollars dans les infrastructures nécessaires pour rivaliser avec SpaceX (SPCX.O) . La société spatiale de Jeff Bezos prévoit également d’ajouter des aires de lancement et d’atterrissage en Floride pour New Glenn, sa fusée orbitale phare à forte capacité d'emport, qui est clouée au sol pour le reste de l’année après avoir explosé en [USN:L6N42608E TEXT:"mai"] sur l’unique pas de tir de l’entreprise. Blue Origin a investi plus de 3 milliards de dollars (2,67 milliards d'euros) à ce jour dans ses vastes installations de production et d’intégration de fusées en Floride, qui emploient quelque 5.000 personnes, précise Ian Richardson, vice-président senior chargé des opérations, dans un article publié sur le blog de l’entreprise. Une extension de ces installations, d’un montant de 330 millions de dollars, permettra de soutenir la production d’une version de la fusée dotée d’une capacité d’emport supérieure, la New Glenn 9x4. Sa mise en service est prévue pour l’été 2027, indique Ian Richardson, ajoutant qu’elle permettra de produire jusqu’à 150 étages supérieurs de fusée par an. "Ces investissements sont axés sur un objectif unique : développer les capacités nécessaires pour soutenir davantage de missions, de manière plus fiable et plus efficace", dit-il. "À plus long terme, ces infrastructures sont conçues pour permettre plusieurs vols par semaine d’ici à la fin de la décennie." L’explosion de la fusée New Glenn en mai, survenue quelques jours avant le lancement prévu de satellites d’Amazon, a gravement endommagé le pas de tir de l’entreprise en Floride, d’où la fusée, haute d'environ 98 mètres, avait décollé à trois reprises depuis son premier vol en 2025. New Glenn devrait reprendre ses vols au début de l’année prochaine.

item.title: UK police assess Palestine Action post by national security adviser's wife
item.description: British police said on Friday they were assessing a social media post after the wife of National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell appeared to express support for Palestine Action, a pro-Palestinian group banned as a terrorist organisation.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: British police said on Friday they were assessing a social media post after the wife of National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell appeared to express support for Palestine Action, a pro-Palestinian group banned as a terrorist organisation. Journalist and author Sarah Helm, who is married to Powell, responded on X to a post about the Irish novelist [USN:L8N4601QN TEXT:"Sally Rooney"], who this week announced her books would no longer be sold in Britain over her plans to use her royalties to support Palestine Action. Helm said in the post: "God help us authors who support Palestine and Palestine Action." In response, a Metropolitan Police spokesperson said the post is "being assessed to determine whether any further police investigation may be required". Palestine Action was proscribed under terrorism laws last year, so expressing support for the group constitutes a criminal offence. Asked for comment, a government spokeswoman said: "These views are held by an individual who does not represent the government in any capacity." Palestine Action has carried out protests including vandalism in support of Palestinian causes, and denies that this amounts to terrorism. [USN:L8N42K0J9 TEXT:"Four members of the group were jailed"] in June over a 2024 raid on a factory operated by Israeli defence firm Elbit which caused more than £1 million of damage. Amnesty International says more than 3,500 people have been arrested in Britain for alleged support of Palestine Action since it was banned last year, many of them for holding up placards. Palestine Action challenged the government's decision to ban the group, but the Court of Appeal ruled in June that the proscription was lawful.

item.title: EEUU firma acuerdo para financiar donaciones a salud materna y neonatal en países más pobres
item.description: El Gobierno de Estados Unidos ha llegado a un acuerdo para seguir suministrando a algunos de los países más pobres del mundo medicamentos y equipos gratuitos que salvan vidas destinados a madres, lactantes y niños pequeños, tras meses de incertidumbre y dificultades en el suministro.
item.dc:creator: Ammu Kannampilly, Jennifer Rigby, Victoire Mukenge
item.content:encoded: El Gobierno de Estados Unidos ha llegado a un acuerdo para seguir suministrando a algunos de los países más pobres del mundo medicamentos y equipos gratuitos que salvan vidas destinados a madres, lactantes y niños pequeños, tras meses de incertidumbre y dificultades en el suministro. La agencia de la ONU para la infancia, UNICEF, se encargará ahora de adquirir estos artículos, según ha comunicado un portavoz del Departamento de Estado a Reuters por correo electrónico, sin dar detalles sobre el acuerdo. UNICEF ha indicado que el acuerdo asciende a 25 millones de dólares y tendrá una duración de un año. Esa suma representa solo una pequeña parte de la ayuda afectada por los recortes de la Administración Trump y el desmantelamiento de la Agencia de los Estados Unidos para el Desarrollo Internacional (USAID). Sin embargo, significa que algunos de los países más vulnerables del mundo no se enfrentarán a otra interrupción brusca de los suministros de los que dependían mientras negocian nuevos acuerdos de ayuda sanitaria con Estados Unidos. Nueve antiguos responsables de ayuda estadounidense, ONG y funcionarios del Gobierno declararon a Reuters que esto había sido motivo de verdadera preocupación, ya que el acuerdo que la ya desaparecida USAID tenía con su contratista debía expirar el mes pasado. ESCASEZ El acuerdo abarca la adquisición y el suministro de material sanitario materno-infantil, así como de algunos productos nutricionales, a al menos 15 países que ya estaban incluidos anteriormente, entre ellos la República Democrática del Congo, Haití y Malí, según ha informado UNICEF. Esto se produce tras casi 18 meses de interrupciones, tras la decisión de Washington de congelar y posteriormente recortar muchos programas de ayuda estadounidenses como parte de su "Estrategia de Salud Global ´America First´". En países como el Congo, la escasez provocada por esta interrupción ya se ha hecho patente sobre el terreno. En el Hospital General de Nyangezi, en el este del Congo, los trabajadores sanitarios afirmaron que se habían quedado sin existencias de medicamentos vitales, como la oxitocina —para prevenir y tratar la hemorragia posparto— y la amoxicilina, un antibiótico de uso pediátrico y durante el parto. "Era una donación que habíamos recibido (anteriormente) de USAID, y en este momento no queda nada", explicó a Reuters la partera Alice Bulambo. El principal almacén gestionado por el Gobierno en la zona lleva más de un año sin existencias, según explicó Olivier Kabarati Amani, director médico de la zona sanitaria de Nyangezi. Como consecuencia, los centros se ven obligados a comprar medicamentos a precios de mercado. En los últimos seis meses, "el coste de la atención sanitaria se ha duplicado, si no triplicado", señaló Amani, en un momento en el que el sistema sanitario del este del Congo ya se enfrenta a la crisis del ébola. El Departamento de Estado de Estados Unidos afirmó que "ha dado prioridad a garantizar que todos los productos esenciales para salvar vidas sigan estando disponibles de forma fiable". TRANSICIÓN Los artículos de salud materna y neonatal representaron menos del 1 % de los más de 5.000 millones de dólares gastados por el programa "Global Health Supply Chain" de la USAID entre 2016 y 2023, según el último informe anual disponible. El gasto se canalizó a través del contratista privado Chemonics. Reuters informó por primera vez en abril sobre los planes de cerrar este programa, que también gestionaba la donación y la entrega de suministros para combatir la malaria y el VIH, y los responsables de la ayuda advirtieron de que el cierre, previsto para el 30 de septiembre, podría provocar escaseces. Los planes para cerrar la cadena de suministro de Chemonics forman parte de la estrategia global de salud de Estados Unidos, cuyo objetivo es que los países avancen hacia la autosuficiencia, al tiempo que se reduce el apoyo estadounidense y la dependencia de los contratistas. En su lugar, Estados Unidos ha firmado más de 30 acuerdos bilaterales de ayuda sanitaria con países receptores, entre ellos el Congo, que requieren cofinanciación por parte de los países y ascienden a miles de millones de dólares en total. Sin embargo, los detalles de los acuerdos aún se están ultimando y, mientras tanto, no estaba claro qué cubriría el vacío en el procedimiento de pedidos. Aunque muchos países ya estaban avanzando hacia la asunción de sus propias necesidades en materia de salud materno-infantil, los plazos de entrega de los pedidos pueden ser de un año o más, según afirmaron cinco antiguos funcionarios de la USAID.

item.title: POINT MARCHÉS L'Europe finit dans le vert, la "tech" pénalise à nouveau le Nasdaq
item.description: Les Bourses européennes ont terminé en hausse vendredi et sur de solides gains hebdomadaires, les indices du Vieux Continent restant largement épargnés par les craintes sur le secteur technologique qui secouent à nouveau Wall Street, et renouent avec un peu de sérénité grâce à la baisse des rendements obligataires.
item.dc:creator: Diana Mandia
item.content:encoded: Les Bourses européennes ont terminé en hausse vendredi et sur de solides gains hebdomadaires, les indices du Vieux Continent restant largement épargnés par les craintes sur le secteur technologique qui secouent à nouveau Wall Street, et renouent avec un peu de sérénité grâce à la baisse des rendements obligataires. À Paris, le CAC 40 (.FCHI) a progressé de 0,28% à 7.956,70 points. À Francfort, le Dax (.GDAXI) a pris 0,94% et à Londres, le FTSE 100 (.FTSE) a avancé de 0,38%. L'indice EuroStoxx 50 (.STOXX50E) a fini sur un gain de 0,57%, le FTSEurofirst 300 (.FTEU3) de 0,69% et le Stoxx 600 (.STOXX) de 0,67%. Sur la semaine, le CAC 40 a pris 1,97%, sa plus forte progression hebdomadaire depuis début août, et le Stoxx 600 a gagné 2,04%, signant à son tour sa meilleure performance depuis début juillet. Le poids moindre du secteur technologique en Europe a permis une séance plutôt constructive, et les investisseurs ont pu se concentrer sur la première vague de résultats d'entreprises du troisième trimestre, avant que le rythme des publications ne s'accélère dans les prochains jours. Les entreprises composant l'indice paneuropéen Stoxx 600 devraient afficher une croissance de leurs résultats trimestriels de plus de 20%, dopée par les entreprises du secteur de l'énergie qui ont bénéficié des perturbations de l'approvisionnement en pétrole provoquées par la guerre au Moyen-Orient et les attaques de drones ukrainiens contre des raffineries russes. Les opérateurs européens font ainsi abstraction en cette fin de semaine des craintes inflationnistes persistantes qui, conjuguées aux inquiétudes budgétaires dans les principales économies mondiales, avaient récemment entraîné une hausse vertigineuse des rendements obligataires. Les risques ne sont pas écartés pour autant: tant la Réserve fédérale (Fed) que la Banque centrale européenne (BCE) devraient, selon les estimations du marché, poursuivre leur resserrement monétaire en décembre, après des pauses respectives ce mois-ci, car les données publiées cette semaine des deux côtés de l'Atlantique montrent en effet que l'inflation ne faiblit pas. Les inquiétudes budgétaires ne s'estompent pas non plus, singulièrement en France où elles devraient resurgir à la faveur du débat parlementaire sur le projet de loi Finances pour 2027, suspendu aux grandes manoeuvres politiques de la campagne pour l'élection présidentielle du printemps prochain. Dans un rapport sur l'Union européenne publié vendredi, le Fonds monétaire international (FMI) [USN:L6N4620PC TEXT:"recommande"] à l'UE de stimuler la croissance ou de réduire son endettement afin de maintenir sa dette sur une trajectoire viable, tout en soulignant que les plans de redressement prévus pourraient ne pas être suffisants. VALEURS À Paris, Schneider Electric (SCHN.PA) a reculé de 1,82%, effaçant ses gains de début de séance, après avoir relevé pour la deuxième fois de l'année ses objectifs de 2026, porté par la demande des géants du cloud pour les centres de données dédiés à l'IA. L'opérateur de satellites Eutelsat (ETL.PA) s'est envolé de 17% alors que l'Ukraine a dû faire face à des restrictions du réseau satellitaire Starlink de SpaceX, ce qui a ravivé l'intérêt des investisseurs pour les alternatives européennes. [USN:L6N462076 TEXT:"Des sources"] ont dit à Reuters que l'ordre de limiter l'utilisation du réseau était venu de la Maison blanche, à un moment où le président américain Donald Trump fait pression sur Kyiv pour qu'il cesse ses attaques contre les raffineries russes. Ailleurs en Europe, le fabricant de puces Aixtron (AIXGn.DE) a progressé de 6% après avoir dépassé les prévisions concernant les prises de commandes au troisième trimestre et confirmé ses prévisions annuelles. Le fabricant d'éoliennes Nordex (NDXG.DE) a bondi de plus de 12% après avoir annoncé un résultat opérationnel du troisième trimestre supérieur aux prévisions et revu à la hausse ses perspectives de marge. Les actions des groupes du secteur automobile, tels que Renault (RENA.PA) , Stellantis (STLAM.MI) , Forvia (FRVIA.PA) ou Valeo (VLOF.PA) , ont pris entre 1,8% et 3,3%, portées par les espoirs que [USN:L6N4620KN TEXT:"l'accord franco-allemand"] sur une "approche commune" améliore les perspectives de cette industrie européenne mise à mal par la concurrence chinoise. A WALL STREET Le secteur technologique continue de peser sur la Bourse de New York, le Nasdaq étant à nouveau affecté par les inquiétudes concernant l'endettement du secteur de l'IA, après une brève accalmie la veille. A l'heure de la clôture en Europe, le Dow Jones (.DJI) gagne 0,07%, mais le Standard & Poor's 500 (.SPX) perd 0,53% et le Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) abandonne 1,26%. L'opérateur de centres de données CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , au coeur de la tempête en raison de sa dette de près de 50 milliards de dollars, recule de 9,4% et dans son sillage Nebius (NBIS.O) perd 8,6%, Applied Digital (APLD.O) 7,2% et Iren (IREN.O) 7,7%. "Il n'y a pas que CoreWeave : plusieurs entreprises entrent dans cette catégorie, car on craint que leurs revenus ne soient tout simplement pas suffisants pour dégager des bénéfices et supporter le niveau d'endettement qu'elles assument", a déclaré Todd Schoenberger, directeur des investissements chez CrossCheck Management. Le secteur des semi-conducteurs perd encore du terrain. Le Nasdaq se dirige ainsi, si la tendance se maintient, vers une forte baisse hebdomadaire, de l'ordre de 4,5%, la plus forte depuis juin. LES INDICATEURS DU JOUR Les prix à l'importation aux États-Unis ont augmenté plus que prévu en septembre, sous l'effet de la hausse des coûts des produits énergétiques et d'une série d'autres biens, ce qui confirme une nouvelle fois la montée des pressions inflationnistes alors que le conflit au Moyen-Orient reste dans l'impasse. Sur un an, ces prix ont progressé de 8,1% en septembre, soit la plus forte hausse depuis juillet 2022, après 6,7% en août. La [USN:L8N4620RU TEXT:"production industrielle"] a pour sa part augmenté de 0,7% en septembre sur un mois, plus fortement que prévu, selon les statistiques officielles publiées vendredi par la Réserve fédérale. Dans la zone euro, l'inflation [USN:ZRN00EOK0 TEXT:"s'est accélérée"] à 3,8% sur un an en septembre, comme précédemment estimé, montrent les données définitives publiées vendredi par Eurostat. TAUX Les obligations souveraines de la zone euro ont connu une semaine solide, les investisseurs s'étant rués sur les obligations d'État face à leurs inquiétudes croissantes concernant l'IA. Le marché retrouve ainsi son rôle de valeur refuge, après les turbulences provoquées par la révision brutale des anticipations en matière de politique monétaire depuis le début de la guerre au Moyen-Orient. Le rendement du Bund allemand à dix ans a fini la séance quasi inchangé, à 3,4093%, tandis que celui du titre à deux ans a perdu 1,8 point de base pour s'établir à 3,0606%. En France, le rendement de l'OAT à dix ans a terminé en légère baisse, à 4,7808%, abandonnant environ 7 points de base sur la semaine. Aux Etats-Unis, les rendements reculent légèrement, celui des Treasuries à dix ans ressortant à 5,0749% et son homologue de l'obligation à deux ans à 4,7210%. CHANGES Le dollar perd 0,37% face à un panier de devises de référence (.DXY) , la baisse des rendements américains ayant rendu le billet vert moins attractif, tandis que les interrogations relatives à l'IA exercent également une pression à la baisse. L'euro gagne 0,29% à 1,1251 dollar EUR=. PÉTROLE Le marché pétrolier évolue sur de faibles variations vendredi mais devrait enregistrer des gains hebdomadaires en raison de l'incertitude concernant les approvisionnements en provenance du Moyen-Orient et d'une baisse plus importante que prévu des stocks de brut aux Etats-Unis la semaine dernière. Le Brent grappille 0,02% à 105,94 dollars le baril et le brut léger américain (West Texas Intermediate, WTI) cède 0,09% à 97,88 dollars. A SUIVRE LE 19 OCTOBRE : [USN:L8N45V0XR] (Certaines données peuvent accuser un léger décalage)

item.title: Pílula de emagrecimento da Eli Lilly recebe aprovação de agência reguladora da UE
item.description: O comitê da Agência Europeia de Medicamentos recomendou nesta sexta-feira a aprovação da pílula para perda de peso Foundayo, da Eli Lilly , o segundo medicamento oral para obesidade a receber o apoio da agência, depois da pílula Wegovy, da Novo Nordisk .
item.dc:creator: Sriparna Roy
item.content:encoded: O comitê da Agência Europeia de Medicamentos recomendou nesta sexta-feira a aprovação da pílula para perda de peso Foundayo, da Eli Lilly (LLY.N) , o segundo medicamento oral para obesidade a receber o apoio da agência, depois da pílula Wegovy, da Novo Nordisk (NOVOb.CO) . A recomendação será agora analisada pela Comissão Europeia antes de esta dar a aprovação final para o lançamento do medicamento na região. Tanto a Novo quanto a Lilly estão em uma corrida para ampliar o acesso aos seus medicamentos orais, visando garantir uma fatia maior de um mercado que deverá ultrapassar US$100 bilhões até 2030. A Foundayo foi lançada nos EUA em abril e no Reino Unido em agosto, e gerou US$98 milhões em vendas no segundo trimestre. A pílula Wegovy, da Novo, gerou US$484,50 milhões no mesmo trimestre. A pílula recebeu aprovação da União Europeia em julho. Ela também está disponível nos EUA, no Reino Unido e nos Emirados Árabes Unidos. Na sexta-feira, a EMA recomendou a autorização de comercialização do Foundayo para o controle de peso e tratamento da diabetes tipo 2 em adultos. A analista da Bernstein, Courtney Breen, prevê que a empresa lançará o medicamento na UE para obesidade por volta do final do ano, acrescentando que, para diabetes, "o momento do lançamento depende do reembolso por parte dos Estados-Membros". A Lilly trabalhará com governos, planos de saúde e sistemas de saúde para ajudar a garantir que as pessoas que possam se beneficiar do Foundayo tenham a oportunidade de acessá-lo, disse Ken Custer, presidente da Lilly Cardiometabolic Health. A pílula, para a qual a Lilly solicitou aprovação em mais de 40 países, contém orforglipron, um agonista do receptor GLP-1 de molécula pequena que pode ajudar a reduzir o apetite e a ingestão de alimentos. Os primeiros dados de prescrição de medicamentos orais para perda de peso nos EUA corroboraram as expectativas de que os comprimidos poderiam expandir o mercado de obesidade, atraindo pacientes que se mostravam relutantes ao uso de injeções. No entanto, a Foundayo teve uma aceitação mais lenta nos EUA em comparação com a Wegovy, da Novo, que foi a primeira a chegar ao mercado. Ao contrário do comprimido Wegovy, o Foundayo pode ser tomado a qualquer hora do dia, sem restrições de alimentos ou água, uma característica que a Lilly destaca como uma vantagem fundamental do medicamento. Ainda não está claro se os pacientes consideram a praticidade do Foundayo suficientemente atraente para impulsionar uma adoção mais ampla.

item.title: Putin says Russia is building non-negotiable 'security zone' in Ukraine along border
item.description: Russia is establishing a "security zone" inside Ukraine along their border, which will be non-negotiable in any future talks with Kyiv, President Vladimir Putin said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russia is establishing a "security zone" inside Ukraine along their border, which will be non-negotiable in any future talks with Kyiv, President Vladimir Putin said on Friday. Putin, wearing military uniform and speaking during a visit to a command post, said the operation was in response to Ukraine's 2024-25 incursion into Russia's western Kursk region. "The Russian armed forces were tasked not only with expelling the enemy from our land but also with establishing a security zone in the adjacent territory. This task is being carried out successfully," he said in televised comments. "Our goal is to ensure the absolute security of Russia’s border regions for the future, and we do not plan to make this a subject for potential peace negotiations with Ukraine." Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the planned security zone spanned 660 km (410 miles), of which 70% was currently under Russia's control. He did not say how deep it would reach inside Ukraine. Putin has spoken before about the need for such a zone but has not previously spelt out the planned extent of it or said it would be off-limits for talks. It requires Russia to carve out land in the Sumy and Kharkiv regions, which are not among those it has claimed as its own territory since launching the war in Ukraine in 2022. Putin, who rarely dons military uniform, struck a hawkish and confident tone in his comments to senior officers. He was speaking at a critical point in diplomacy over the war , one week after a [USN:L4N45Y0AR TEXT:"deal"] to sell Russian diesel to the US that has won favour with President Donald Trump and prompted a new souring of the relationship between Trump and Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskiy. Putin said Russian forces had yet to capture just over 10% of the territory of Ukraine's Donetsk region, a key objective, and 16.5% of the Zaporizhzhia region. He praised the effectiveness of Russian strikes against Ukrainian military, industrial and logistics targets, while adding there was still room for improvement in Russia's own air defences. Ukrainian drones have attacked several Russian data centres and a big oil refinery in the past nine days, while Russia has continued to pound Ukrainian cities, power plants and ports, among other targets. Earlier, Putin's investment envoy Kirill Dmitriev said Russia and the US were discussing a range of new joint projects including [USN:L1N4620KW TEXT:"nuclear-powered data centres"] in the wake of last week's agreement on diesel.

item.title: Indonesia faces rare MSCI exclusion that could cut it off from global capital
item.description: A warning from MSCI that it may exclude Indonesia from its stock market indexes — benchmarks used by global financial investors — risks cutting the nation off from international capital and relegating it to an investment backwater.
item.dc:creator: Ankur Banerjee, Yantoultra Ngui, Karin Strohecker
item.content:encoded: A warning from MSCI that it may exclude Indonesia from its stock market indexes — benchmarks used by global financial investors — risks cutting the nation off from international capital and relegating it to an investment backwater. MSCI [USN:L4N46124S TEXT:"stunned investors"] by proposing that it remove Indonesia from its global stock indexes altogether, months after floating a less severe downgrade from emerging market to frontier over opaque ownership and securities trading practices. A cut to standalone status would be unusually harsh and rare: Argentina was dropped in 2021 for imposing capital controls, and Russia in 2022 after Western sanctions cut it off from global finance over its invasion of Ukraine. Indonesia would find itself in a small group of standalone markets that includes Lebanon and Zimbabwe. Indonesia has been an MSCI emerging market since 1989, and a downgrade of the proposed magnitude would be a huge reversal for a market that until recently was a foreign investor favourite. Removing the country from major global benchmarks that steer billions of dollars in foreign investment could hurt far more than just its stock market. "The proposal ... goes well beyond what we had considered our worst-case scenario," said Rully Arya Wisnubroto, head of research at Mirae Asset Sekuritas in Jakarta. The [USN:L4N4620NX TEXT:"MSCI announcement wiped"] about $65 billion off the value of Indonesian equities, with an 11.6% drop on the Jakarta Composite Index (.JKSE) — its biggest one-day fall since the Asian financial crisis in 1998. The shock spread beyond equities, with the rupiah falling as much as 0.8% and some analysts raising the possibility of a central bank interest rate hike on Tuesday, when rates had been expected to stay on hold. "The purpose (of a rate hike) would be pre-emptive, i.e. in order to prevent the expected equity foreign outflows from widening to the fixed income side as well as being exacerbated by resident capital outflows," Citi wrote in a note to clients. Unlike a downgrade to frontier status, a move to [USN:L6N4620AP TEXT:"standalone"] would provide no offsetting demand from frontier-index funds, leaving passive emerging-market money heading for the exits. Banks estimate the move could trigger $3 billion to $6 billion in passive outflows, with JPMorgan putting the figure at $4.8 billion and UBS warning active investors could pull another $15 billion. More than $1.8 trillion in assets are benchmarked to MSCI's emerging-market indexes, according to the index provider's website. INDONESIA INDEX WEIGHT AMPLIFIES IMPACT Indonesia, Southeast Asia's biggest economy, is the world's top exporter of thermal coal, palm oil and nickel and a major supplier of copper and coffee. While the country has benefited from rising prices of some of its top commodity exports this year, as a net oil importer, its import bills have also soared. The fallout from the stock index exclusion could also spread to Indonesia's public finances should state-linked companies find it harder or more expensive to raise money, potentially forcing the government to take spending back onto its own books or scale back investment, Citi analysts added. "We expect the broader economic impact to be predominantly indirect, with external financing representing the most immediate transmission channel," said Irman Faiz, economist at Bank Danamon Indonesia in Jakarta. Indonesia's removal would involve significantly more index-linked money than previous cases, despite its weight shrinking from 1.2% at the end of 2025 to 0.46% now, according to JPMorgan. When Argentina was removed, its weighting stood at 0.12%. "Is Indonesia really on par with Zimbabwe in market behaviour and structure? Is shareholder treatment really worse than in many other EM markets, including several in Asia?" said Juan Torres, co-manager of the Neuberger Emerging Markets Equity fund. MSCI cited opaque ownership, suspected coordinated trading and inadequate enforcement, saying the problems undermine investors' ability to determine companies' true free float and rely on market prices. The index provider expects the downgrade to go ahead unless a consultation running until next April finds clear evidence of improved governance and market functioning. A final decision is due by next June. [USN:L6N4620JP TEXT:"Indonesian authorities"] have spent much of the year trying to address MSCI's concerns, tightening disclosure requirements and laying out plans to raise minimum free floats. On Friday, the regulator also announced sanctions linked to alleged manipulation in three stocks. "It’s true that MSCI has a strong reputation, and it’s also true that we need to pay attention to what they say," said Dradjad Hari Wibowo, the deputy coordinating minister for economic affairs. "But there’s one thing I want to emphasize — they (MSCI) aren’t always right."

item.title: Arizona approves state's first non-ABA accredited law school
item.description: The Arizona Supreme Court has approved the state's first law school not accredited by the American Bar Association, a move the court said would help address Arizona's lawyer shortage.
item.dc:creator: Karen Sloan
item.content:encoded: The Arizona Supreme Court has approved the state's first law school not accredited by the American Bar Association, a move the court said would help address Arizona's lawyer shortage. The court's approval on Thursday of Grand Canyon University Law School, which is slated to open as early as fall 2027, means its graduates will be eligible to take Arizona's bar exam and apply to become licensed to practice in the state. Grand Canyon law graduates would largely be limited to Arizona under current attorney licensing rules in other states that require graduation from an ABA-accredited law school, though some states have begun to relax that provision. Officials at the private, Christian university said the school plans to pursue ABA accreditation but that Arizona's recognition will give it more flexibility amid potential changes to the bar association's status as the federally recognized accreditor of law schools. The US Department of Education under President Donald Trump is [USN:L6N44I0V8 TEXT:"poised to revoke"] the ABA's accreditor status, and five Republican-controlled states including Texas and Florida have [USN:L6N45R0V5 TEXT:"moved to end"] their near-exclusive reliance on the ABA in attorney admissions. James Williams, the founding dean of Grand Canyon's law school, in a statement said the school is grateful for the Arizona Supreme Court's "willingness to consider an innovative approach to legal education and for the opportunity to demonstrate that a new pathway to licensure can maintain the highest standards of academic excellence." The court said it is not accepting approval requests from other non-ABA-accredited law schools while it assesses how its new approach is working. Grand Canyon, located in Phoenix, unveiled plans for its new law school in August, saying it will "integrate the Christian worldview throughout its curriculum while emphasizing Constitutional law, free-market principles and the rule of law." Grand Canyon will be the state's third law school alongside Arizona State University Sandra Day O'Connor College of Law and the University of Arizona James E. Rogers College of Law, both of which are accredited by the ABA. A 2020 study by the ABA found that Arizona was tied with South Carolina and Arkansas for the lowest ratio of active attorneys per capita, with just 2.1 attorneys for every 1,000 Arizonans. The national average was roughly four lawyers per 1,000 residents. The Arizona Supreme Court in 2024 established the [USN:L1N3JA0WC TEXT:"Arizona Lawyers Apprentice Program"], a first-of-its-kind effort that gives law school graduates who fall just short of passing the state's bar exam the option to become licensed attorneys after spending two years working under the supervision of a lawyer in a rural area or a government or nonprofit law setting. Read more: [USN:L6N44I0V8 TEXT:"Trump administration moves to end attorney group's law school oversight"] [USN:L1N3JA0WC TEXT:"To boost lawyer numbers in 'legal deserts,' Arizona adopts apprentice plan for bar exam failers"]

item.title: Real Madrid demand resignation of LaLiga chief after Nazi propaganda comparison
item.description: Real Madrid demanded the resignation of LaLiga President Javier Tebas on Friday after he compared rhetoric from the club's management to the propaganda methods used by the Nazi Party in Germany.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Real Madrid demanded the resignation of LaLiga President Javier Tebas on Friday after he compared rhetoric from the club's management to the propaganda methods used by the Nazi Party in Germany. Tebas wrote earlier on Friday on social media that "Real Madrid’s management directs an orchestra of mouthpieces and Real Madrid TV leads the singing." The LaLiga president was responding to articles by two journalists saying he and LaLiga were acting against Real's interests. Tebas added that the authors in the El Debate newspaper were amplifying a message on behalf of Real's management. Reuters has asked El Debate for comment. Real Madrid's demand for Tebas to immediately resign deepens a feud between the club and La Liga's chief. Real in September [USN:L6N45E0RN TEXT:"called for a new LaLiga president"] in response to Tebas calling their complaints about refereeing decisions 'a smokescreen' for their shortcomings on the pitch. Tebas on Friday criticised Real Madrid TV's coverage of officiating at their matches. "Their score is always the same: select the plays that suit them, repeat the grievance, feed the suspicion, and point fingers at the enemies," he wrote. "That method recalls propaganda mechanisms used by Goebbels, Nazi Germany's Minister of Propaganda. "The comparison is with those propaganda techniques, not with an ideology or, of course, with the Madridista fanbase," added LaLiga's president. REAL DEMAND TEBAS RESIGNATION Real Madrid released a statement later on Friday demanding that Tebas resign from his positions as LaLiga chief and vice-president of the Royal Spanish Football Federation. The statement called it "intolerable and extraordinarily serious" that Tebas used "a comparison with the propaganda methods of the Nazi regime to discredit our club, its management and its television. "Tebas' repeated conduct demonstrates a lack of neutrality, respect and impartiality incompatible with his institutional responsibilities," said Real. "It is unacceptable that he even takes advantage of questions, information or opinions from journalists unrelated to the club to direct his accusations at us, attributing to us actions of third parties for which we bear no responsibility." The 64-year-old Tebas, who is elected by the 42 professional clubs in Spain's top two tiers, has been LaLiga president since 2013. In 2023, he was reelected unopposed until 2027. Real Madrid's statement came hours after LaLiga confirmed that they are one of the six clubs that will sit on the league's Executive Committee this season.

item.title: Judge rejects CFTC, Gemini bid to vacate $5 million settlement
item.description: A federal judge in Manhattan has rejected a joint request by the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission and Gemini, a cryptocurrency exchange founded by twin brothers Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss, to undo a $5 million settlement from the Biden administration.
item.dc:creator: Mike Scarcella
item.content:encoded: A federal judge in Manhattan has rejected a joint request by the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission and Gemini, a cryptocurrency exchange founded by twin brothers Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss, to undo a $5 million settlement from the Biden administration. In a ruling on Thursday, US District Judge Alvin Hellerstein said the agency and Gemini Trust Co had not met the standards required to set aside the settlement, which resolved a lawsuit over statements Gemini made during the agency's review of a proposed bitcoin futures contract. The CFTC and a lawyer for Gemini did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The CFTC sued Gemini in 2022, alleging the company made false or misleading statements during the agency's review of the proposed futures product. The January 2025 settlement came at the end of Democratic President Joe Biden’s administration and shortly before a trial. Republican President Donald Trump’s administration has taken a friendlier, [USN:L2N3QM0E3 TEXT:"narrower approach"] to crypto sector enforcement. The commodities agency and Gemini in May jointly asked Hellerstein, appointed by Democratic President Bill Clinton, to wipe out the [USN:L1N3O20Q6 TEXT:"settlement and court order"]. They said in a filing that the agency’s complaint, lodged in 2022, would not have been filed under new enforcement policy priorities and standards under Trump. The court filing said regulators should not have [USN:L1N2XP1OS TEXT:"accused"] Gemini of making false statements in connection with its bitcoin futures business. The CFTC and Gemini said the CFTC had "resorted to inappropriate tactics" to bring a lawsuit. Gemini agreed not to receive a refund on the $5 million penalty if the settlement were vacated. Hellerstein said Gemini had litigated against the CFTC for more than three years before voluntarily agreeing to settle and that the agency's current view of the case does not require vacating the settlement. The Winklevoss twins became widely known after accusing Mark Zuckerberg of stealing their idea for Facebook, a dispute that ended with a 2008 settlement that included cash and company stock.

item.title: Putin agrees to cooperate with Pope Leo's plea for aid for Ukrainian town
item.description: President Vladimir Putin told Pope Leo he had agreed to cooperate after the pontiff asked him on Friday to help get vital supplies into the Russian-controlled Ukrainian town of Oleshky, the Kremlin said.
item.dc:creator: Joshua McElwee
item.content:encoded: President Vladimir Putin told Pope Leo he had agreed to cooperate after the pontiff asked him on Friday to help get vital supplies into the Russian-controlled Ukrainian town of Oleshky, the Kremlin said. Leo phoned Putin and asked him to arrange a ceasefire to let aid and food into the town, taken by Russian forces in February 2022, the Vatican said. Residents have reported [USN:L8N45K1N1 TEXT:"a deepening food crisis"]. Leo expressed "deep concern" over the humanitarian situation there, the Vatican added. Russia and Ukraine accuse each other of blocking supplies to the town, which Ukrainian forces want to retake. "The Vatican’s intention to help create the conditions necessary to ensure the safety of the town’s population and to organise vital supplies has been supported," the Kremlin said in a statement. It did not mention a ceasefire. "It has been agreed to cooperate on this matter," it added. Leo and Putin are known to have spoken once previously, in June 2025. The pope also reaffirmed the Holy See's commitment to any initiatives for peace, the Vatican said. The pope, 71, is recovering at Rome's Gemelli hospital after surgery for lung cancer. The Vatican said earlier on Friday that he is [USN:L8N46210T TEXT:"showing steady improvement"] and is able to work and do normal daily activities. The Kremlin said Putin had wished Leo a speedy and full recovery. The Vatican's Secretary of State, Cardinal Pietro Parolin, told reporters after the call that it had been Leo's initiative. The pope, he said, wanted "to plead the cause of this besieged city". Russia has acknowledged critical problems with food and medical supplies in Oleshky and said its military was working to resolve them. It blamed Ukraine for the crisis, saying it was obstructing those supplies from getting to the town. Ukraine has said it is Russia which is thwarting food deliveries. Oleshky, in Ukraine's Kherson region, had a pre-war population of some 24,000, and is still home to around 1,700 residents, including 47 children, according to Danielle Bell, head of the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine.

item.title: Putin told Pope Leo he backs Vatican idea to help civilians in Oleshky, Kremlin says
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin told Pope Leo in a phone call on Friday that he supported a Vatican initiative to help deliver supplies to civilians in the Russian-controlled town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine and was ready to cooperate on the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russian President Vladimir Putin told Pope Leo in a phone call on Friday that he supported a Vatican initiative to help deliver supplies to civilians in the Russian-controlled town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine and was ready to cooperate on the matter. The Vatican said earlier on Friday that Leo had urged Putin to agree to a truce to allow the entry of first aid and food supplies into the town and to permit a voluntary evacuation of the civilian population. Russia and Ukraine both accuse each other of blocking supplies to the population of the town which Ukrainian forces want to retake. "The Vatican’s intention to help create the conditions necessary to ensure the safety of the town’s population and to organise vital supplies has been supported," the Kremlin said in a statement. "It has been agreed to cooperate on this matter."

item.title: Morocco's new government has new finance minister, keeps foreign, interior ministers unchanged
item.description: Morocco's football federation chief and former budget minister Fouzi Lekjaa was appointed economy and finance minister in the country's new government that was formed following the September 23 parliamentary elections, state news agency MAP reported.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Eljechtimi
item.content:encoded: Morocco's football federation chief and former budget minister Fouzi Lekjaa was appointed economy and finance minister in the country's new government that was formed following the September 23 [USN:L8N45G056 TEXT:"parliamentary elections"], state news agency MAP reported. Lekjaa, a member of the liberal-centrist Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM), joins a 32-member government led by Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, whom King Mohammed VI [USN:L8N45G056 TEXT:"appointed"] last month as the country's first woman head of government after PAM won the largest share of seats in parliament. PAM [USN:L1N45Y0PZ TEXT:"formed a coalition"] with moderate socialist parties PPS and USFP and the nationalist Istiqlal. Together they hold 207 seats in parliament, above the 198 needed for a majority. The new government retained the foreign affairs and interior ministers in their posts, MAP reported following the government appointment ceremony chaired by King Mohammed VI. The lineup also retained the ministers responsible for justice, water, defence, industry and transport. Among the newcomers, PPS leader Nabil Benabdallah returned to government as education minister, while fellow PPS member Charafat Afailal was named energy minister. Other newcomers included Khalid Hatimi as minister of agriculture, maritime fisheries and food sovereignty. The new government will oversee the final stages of a $20-billion push to prepare for [USN:L1N42004C TEXT:"the 2030 World Cup"], which Morocco will co-host with Portugal and Spain. It [USN:L6N4580D4 TEXT:"faces pressure"] to address unemployment and demands for better education and health services, which fuelled the youth [USN:L6N3VN095 TEXT:"Gen Z protests"] last year and the [USN:L1N43Y04J TEXT:"Ceuta migration crisis"] in July. [USN:L6N4580D4 TEXT:"The new government"], however, is not expected to change policy direction in Morocco, a constitutional monarchy where the king retains sweeping powers over foreign policy and defense.

item.title: Austin FC sign top scorer Christian Ramirez to new deal
item.description: Austin FC signed top scorer Christian Ramirez to a new guaranteed contract through the end of the 2027-28 season on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Austin FC signed top scorer Christian Ramirez to a new guaranteed contract through the end of the 2027-28 season on Friday. The 35-year-old forward has tallied nine goals and two assists in 25 regular-season matches (14 starts) this season. The nine-year MLS veteran and former MLS Cup champion signed with Austin in February 2026. "At the start of this season, I didn't know where I'd be playing. Looking back on it now, Austin FC was the perfect place for me to land," he said. "I'm grateful to have had the opportunity to come in and make an impact both on and off the pitch. I know there are big things ahead for the Club. It's an amazing organization with amazing people and fans. I'm happy that my family and I will be staying in Austin." Ramirez has recorded 64 goals and 23 assists in 210 career MLS matches (135 starts) with Minnesota United (2017-18), LAFC (2018-19), Houston Dynamo (2019-21), Columbus Crew (2023-24), LA Galaxy (2025) and Austin. He won a championship with the Crew in 2023. "Christian has earned this new contract through his performances and the qualities he brings to our group every day," chief soccer officer Khaled El-Ahmad said. "He scores important goals, leads by example, and brings the professionalism and character we want at Austin FC. We're pleased to keep him here, and we believe he has an important role to play as we strengthen the team and raise our standards." --Field Level Media

item.title: Gobernador del Banco de Japón promete seguir subiendo tasas y mantener inflación en torno a objetivo
item.description: El gobernador del Banco de Japón, Kazuo Ueda, afirmó el viernes que la entidad se centrará en mantener la inflación subyacente en torno a su objetivo del 2% y no tolerará ningún rebasamiento, subrayando una vez más su determinación de seguir subiendo las tasas de interés.
item.dc:creator: Leika Kihara
item.content:encoded: El gobernador del Banco de Japón, Kazuo Ueda, afirmó el viernes que la entidad se centrará en mantener la inflación subyacente en torno a su objetivo del 2% y no tolerará ningún rebasamiento, subrayando una vez más su determinación de seguir subiendo las tasas de interés. Ueda señaló asimismo que los datos nacionales recientes y las conversaciones que mantuvo con autoridades monetarias de todo el mundo en las reuniones del FMI de esta semana indican que la evolución de la economía y los precios se ajusta, en líneas generales, a las previsiones del banco central. "Como la inflación subyacente se sitúa más o menos cerca de nuestro objetivo del 2%, no podemos tolerar que la inflación se acelere aún más", afirmó en una rueda de prensa celebrada en Bangkok. "Nuestra postura ha cambiado recientemente hacia una fase en la que mantener la inflación en torno a nuestro objetivo del 2% se ha convertido en nuestro principal objetivo de política monetaria". Estas declaraciones se produjeron antes de la reunión clave sobre política monetaria del BoJ prevista para finales de mes, en la que el consejo elaborará nuevas previsiones trimestrales de crecimiento e inflación que serán analizadas al detalle en busca de pistas sobre el ritmo y el momento de futuras alzas de tasas. "Dado que la inflación subyacente se sitúa bastante cerca del 2%, cada vez es más importante que antes mantenerla en torno a nuestro objetivo", señaló Ueda, añadiendo que el banco tendría en cuenta este aspecto en su próxima reunión de política monetaria. Ueda se llevará consigo las conclusiones de sus conversaciones con sus homólogos del G7 y del G20 en Bangkok, entre ellas lo que su homólogo estadounidense, Kevin Warsh, describió como el "reto común" al que se enfrentan las autoridades monetarias mundiales a la hora de abordar la inflación. El BoJ podría enfrentarse a nuevas presiones para acelerar el ritmo de las alzas de tasas en medio de las presiones inflacionistas mundiales derivadas de la guerra de Irán y de una perturbación de la demanda impulsada por la inteligencia artificial, asuntos que dominaron los debates en las reuniones del FMI de esta semana. Tras haber subido las tasas en septiembre, muchos miembros del Banco de Japón prefieren mantener la situación tal y como está en su reunión del 29 al 30 de octubre, a la espera de más datos sobre cómo han afectado hasta ahora sus alzas a las condiciones económicas y financieras, según informaron fuentes a Reuters. Aun así, es probable que la entidad emita señales agresivas sobre las perspectivas de política monetaria que dejen margen para un aumento en diciembre, y los analistas señalan que la IA se suma a las presiones inflacionistas derivadas de los altos costos energéticos y del aumento de los precios de las importaciones por la debilidad del yen. "Tras haber hablado con autoridades monetarias de todo el mundo, no me dio la impresión de que sus opiniones divergieran mucho de las nuestras", afirmó Ueda sobre las presiones inflacionistas globales. "Pero me pareció que más de ellos consideran que la demanda mundial de IA es algo más fuerte de lo previsto por el BoJ".

item.title: US strikes one-year deal to fund maternal and newborn health donations in poorest countries
item.description: The US government has struck a deal to continue supplying some of the world's poorest nations with free life-saving medication and equipment for mothers, infants and young children, after months of uncertainty and challenges with supply.
item.dc:creator: Ammu Kannampilly, Jennifer Rigby, Victoire Mukenge
item.content:encoded: The US government has struck a deal to continue supplying some of the world's poorest nations with free life-saving medication and equipment for mothers, infants and young children, after [USN:L6N40L0RM TEXT:"months of uncertainty"] and challenges with supply. The UN children's agency UNICEF will now procure these items, a State department spokesperson told Reuters by email, without giving details of the arrangement. UNICEF said the agreement is worth $25 million and will last for one year. That sum represents only a small part of the aid affected by the Trump administration's cuts and dismantling of the US Agency for International Development (USAID). But it means that some of the world's most vulnerable nations will not face another abrupt disruption to supplies they relied on while they work on new health aid deals with the US. Nine former US aid officials, NGOs and government officials told Reuters that this had been a real concern because the deal the now-defunct USAID had with its contractor was due to run out last month. SHORTAGES The agreement covers the procurement and delivery of maternal and child health supplies, as well as some nutrition supplies, to at least 15 countries previously covered, including Democratic Republic of Congo, Haiti and Mali, UNICEF said. It follows almost 18 months of disruption after Washington's move to freeze and then scale back [USN:L2N3PI0VN TEXT:"many US aid programmes"] as part of its "America First Global Health Strategy". In countries such as Congo, shortages due to the disruption have already been showing up on the ground. At the Nyangezi General Hospital in eastern Congo, health workers said they had run out of supplies of life-saving medications including oxytocin to prevent and treat post-partum haemorrhage and amoxicillin, an antibiotic for paediatric use and during childbirth. "It was a donation we received (previously) from USAID, and at the moment, there is none," midwife Alice Bulambo told Reuters. The main government-run warehouse in the area has faced stockouts for over a year, said Olivier Kabarati Amani, chief medical officer for Nyangezi health zone. As a result, facilities are forced to buy medicines at market prices. Over the last six months, "the cost of care has doubled, if not tripled," Amani said, at a time when the healthcare system in eastern Congo is [USN:L6N45L142 TEXT:"already struggling"] with Ebola. The US State Department said it "has prioritized ensuring all life-saving commodities have continued to be made reliably available." TRANSITION Maternal and newborn health items amounted to less than 1% of the more than $5 billion spent by the USAID Global Health Supply Chain program between 2016 and 2023, according to the most recently available annual report. The spending was channelled through private contractor Chemonics. Reuters [USN:L6N40L0RM TEXT:"first reported"] on plans to close this programme, which also managed the donation and delivery of supplies to tackle malaria and HIV, in April, with aid officials warning that the September 30 shutdown could cause shortages. The plans to close the Chemonics supply chain are part of the broader US global health strategy, which aims to move countries towards self-reliance alongside scaled-back US support and reduced reliance on contractors. The US has instead signed more than 30 bilateral deals on health aid with recipient countries, including Congo, which require co-financing from the countries and are worth billions of dollars in total. But the details of the deals are still being worked out and it had been unclear what would fill the gap in the ordering procedure in the meantime. While many nations were already moving towards taking over their maternal and child health needs, lead times for orders can be a year or more, five former USAID officials said. The Congolese government aims to take over by next year, but has struggled with the recent uncertainty, said Polydor Kabila, coordinator of the universal healthcare programme in the president’s office. Alongside the UNICEF deal, the US authorities have extended the deadline for Chemonics deliveries of some key malaria and HIV items, the State Department spokesperson told Reuters. The US has also signed a deal with the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria to allow countries to order new US-funded HIV and malaria supplies through the Fund's order platform. In a statement, UNICEF said it would work with the US to "keep health and nutrition supplies moving so more children receive life-saving care," adding that no orders have yet been placed but are expected shortly.

item.title: Video de amenaza en vuelo de easyJet en julio de 2025 se comparte como si fuera reciente
item.description: Un video de pasajeros en el que reducen a un hombre después de que gritara "Muerte a Estados Unidos", "Muerte a Trump" y "Allahu Akbar" a bordo de un vuelo de easyJet en julio de 2025 se comparte erróneamente etiquetado en línea como si fuera un incidente en septiembre de 2026.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Un video de pasajeros en el que reducen a un hombre después de que gritara "Muerte a Estados Unidos", "Muerte a Trump" y "Allahu Akbar" a bordo de un vuelo de easyJet en julio de 2025 se comparte erróneamente etiquetado en línea como si fuera un incidente en septiembre de 2026. Estos son los detalles clave: Una publicación del 30 de septiembre en X dice que el video fue grabado “hoy temprano” a bordo de un vuelo doméstico de easyJet en Reino Unido. Un usuario en la red social X publicó el mismo video el 27 de julio de 2025, dijo que un amigo suyo lo había grabado y que el incidente había ocurrido en un vuelo de easyJet esa mañana. La Policía de Escocia informó en un comunicado que arrestó y presentó cargos contra un hombre de 41 años tras un disturbio en un vuelo con destino a Glasgow en la mañana de ese día. Un portavoz de easyJet dijo que ese día la policía retiró a un pasajero del vuelo EZY609 de Luton a Glasgow “debido a su comportamiento a bordo”, reportó la emisora televisiva local STV. Abhay Nayak compareció ante el Tribunal del Comisario de Paisley el 28 de julio acusado de agresión y de poner en peligro la seguridad del avión tras el incidente ocurrido en el vuelo. No se declaró culpable ni inocente y quedó en prisión preventiva, informaron STV y otros medios de comunicación. Un portavoz de easyJet dijo a Reuters en un correo electrónico que no se ha producido ningún incidente similar en un vuelo de la aerolínea en septiembre de 2026. Reuters no halló evidencia de un incidente reportado en un vuelo de easyJet ese mes. Un sitio web de terceros sobre actividad judicial muestra una audiencia aplazada del 5 de octubre de este año en el Tribunal Superior de Glasgow, bajo el nombre de “Abhay Devdas Nayak”, como el procedimiento más reciente en el caso de 2025. La Oficina de la Corona y Servicio del Procurador Fiscal dijo a Reuters que el caso está programado para una audiencia preliminar el 18 de noviembre en el Tribunal Superior de Glasgow. La Policía de Escocia no respondió a una solicitud de comentarios. Veredicto: Erróneamente etiquetado. El video se grabó en un incidente que ocurrió en julio de 2025 en un vuelo de la aerolínea easyJet, no en septiembre de 2026. Reuters Fact Check ofrece información confiable mediante su canal de WhatsApp para México . Envíenos un mensaje con el contenido en español que desea que verifiquemos. Este artículo fue realizado por el equipo de Reuters Fact Check. Lea más sobre nuestro trabajo de verificación de afirmaciones en las redes sociales.

item.title: Papa León mantiene conversación telefónica con Putin, expresa preocupación por situación en Oleshky
item.description: El papa León mantuvo el viernes una conversación telefónica con el presidente ruso, Vladímir Putin, informó el Vaticano, en la que expresó su "profunda preocupación" por la situación humanitaria en la localidad ucraniana de Oleshky, ocupada por las fuerzas de Moscú.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El papa León mantuvo el viernes una conversación telefónica con el presidente ruso, Vladímir Putin, informó el Vaticano, en la que expresó su "profunda preocupación" por la situación humanitaria en la localidad ucraniana de Oleshky, ocupada por las fuerzas de Moscú. León instó a Putin a establecer una tregua para permitir la entrada de ayuda de emergencia y suministros alimentarios en la localidad, señaló el Vaticano, así como para permitir la evacuación voluntaria de la población civil.

item.title: Empleados Meta dicen cuentas de Lula se vieron limitadas durante elecciones Brasil: Folha
item.description: Empleados de Meta reconocieron en comunicaciones internas que las cuentas de Instagram del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva se vieron afectadas negativamente por las restricciones impuestas durante las elecciones de Brasil, informó el viernes el periódico "Folha de S.Paulo", citando mensajes a los que tuvo acceso.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Empleados de Meta reconocieron en comunicaciones internas que las cuentas de Instagram del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva se vieron afectadas negativamente por las restricciones impuestas durante las elecciones de Brasil, informó el viernes el periódico "Folha de S.Paulo", citando mensajes a los que tuvo acceso. Según el informe, los mensajes también reconocían que la plataforma recomendaba el perfil del candidato opositor, el senador Flávio Bolsonaro, así como su canal de WhatsApp. Meta (META.O) no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. Lula se enfrentará a Bolsonaro en un balotaje el 25 de octubre, tras el resultado, mejor de lo esperado, obtenido por el senador en la primera vuelta celebrada a principios de este mes. El equipo de Lula afirmó a principios de esta semana que presentaría una denuncia ante la Organización de los Estados Americanos alegando que Meta, propietaria de Instagram, WhatsApp y Facebook, manipuló las redes sociales durante las elecciones de Brasil. Según el partido de Lula, algunas de sus publicaciones aparecieron sin botón para compartir, sufrieron una reducción de su alcance y presentaban historias que impedían las reacciones y el intercambio, además de aparecer sin audio o reproducirse a velocidad acelerada. Un magistrado del máximo tribunal electoral de Brasil ordenó el jueves a la empresa que no limitara injustificadamente el alcance del contenido político relacionado con ambos candidatos hasta el final de la campaña de la segunda vuelta. La resolución también estipulaba que Meta AI, el chatbot de inteligencia artificial de la empresa, no debe favorecer a ninguno de los candidatos a la hora de generar contenido relacionado con las elecciones.

item.title: Chinese online retailer Temu agrees to data privacy restrictions to settle Texas lawsuit, documents say
item.description: Chinese online retailer Temu has agreed to settle data privacy claims raised by Texas and will restrict how it handles personal data from shoppers in the state, according to documents made public Friday.
item.dc:creator: Jody Godoy, David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: Chinese online retailer Temu has agreed to settle data privacy claims raised by Texas and will restrict how it handles personal data from shoppers in the state, according to documents made public Friday. Temu faces several lawsuits from US states concerned that the company unlawfully harvests US user data that could be accessed by the Chinese government. Texas is the first to resolve those claims. It is also the first time the company has agreed to keep personal data on US servers and restrict when it can be sent to China, Texas officials said. Temu also agreed to conduct annual independent product safety testing to identify products containing dangerous chemicals and materials. Temu must remove any products found to contain dangerous materials, terminate the seller and its affiliated stores, notify affected Texas consumers, and issue full refunds. Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton said the settlement also requires Temu "to implement rigorous new product audits and safety standards to protect consumers from dangerous materials in products, including clothing and children’s items." He added it will prevent Temu from collecting and using Americans' data. Temu had more than 82.4 million active users in the United States as of September 2023, Paxton's office said. Temu will pay $3 million to the state as part of the settlement and Texas said failure to abide by various data security provisions would result in a potential $8 million penalty each year a violation occurs. Several states sued Temu in the wake of reports alleging Temu and parent company PDD Holdings < PDD.O > used invasive mechanisms in their apps. Temu, which did not immediately respond to a request for comment, denied wrongdoing in the settlement documents, and will also be required to hire a third party cybersecurity auditor to examine the app’s code for malware and spyware, one of the main concerns that spurred Texas to sue in February. Under the terms of the settlement, Temu agreed to send only data necessary to fulfilling a transaction, such as shipping addresses, to China. Texas alleged that Temu used code that allows an inappropriate level of access to users’ devices. Temu has denied the allegations.

item.title: Edited image of transgender councillor shared online
item.description: An image of a transgender Green Party councillor in Britain has been edited to give her more masculine features.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: An image of a transgender Green Party councillor in Britain has been edited to give her more masculine features. The altered image, shared on X and Facebook , shows Eden Hills, councillor for Little London and Woodhouse , in the northern English city of Leeds, with facial hair. The original image was a screenshot taken from a video uploaded to the Leeds Green Party’s Instagram account on May 8, in which Hills delivers a speech upon being elected as a representative for the ward. That does not show a moustache. Reuters analysed the altered photo with Google’s SynthID, an AI detection tool, which concluded the image was created using the tech company's generative AI models. The tool works by detecting a hidden watermark contained in AI-generated or AI-modified images created by Google models. Hills also told Reuters in a phone call on October 14 that the image is not genuine. Hills was elected as councillor for the Green Party on May 7 with 2,617 votes , more than half of the votes cast among six candidates, according to Leeds City Council. Verdict: Misleading. The image is altered to depict Hills with an added moustache. This article was produced by the Reuters Fact Check team. Read more  about our fact-checking work.

item.title: Russia's Rosatom targets year-end nuclear start-up at Turkey's Akkuyu
item.description: Russia's state nuclear corporation Rosatom expects the first reactor at Turkey's Akkuyu nuclear power plant to achieve its first self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction before the end of this year, Rosatom head Alexei Likhachev said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russia's state nuclear corporation Rosatom expects the first reactor at Turkey's Akkuyu nuclear power plant to achieve its first self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction before the end of this year, Rosatom head Alexei Likhachev said on Friday. "We remain on track for the planned physical start-up in the second half of December... We hope that before the end of the year the Turkish unit will transition from the construction phase to the start-up phase," he said. Moscow and Ankara signed an agreement in 2010 to build a nuclear power plant with four Russian VVER-1200 reactors, but the project has faced repeated delays and bureaucratic hurdles. Rosatom began construction of the Akkuyu plant in 2018. The commissioning schedule has been repeatedly pushed back from its original 2023 target. After Moscow launched military action in Ukraine in 2022, pressure on the project increased. Although Rosatom was not targeted by Western sanctions, risks related to payments and other issues remain. Physical start-up involves fuel loading and achieving first criticality, the reactor's first self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction. The next major milestone is grid connection and the start of electricity generation. Likhachev also reported progress in talks with potential partners for the Akkuyu. He said he had discussed the matter the previous day with Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar, who attended the Russian Energy Week forum. "We have developed a menu of possible arrangements for a Turkish investor. The choice is primarily up to the Turkish government. I hope that following our meeting, Mr Bayraktar will brief the country's leadership and that the right decisions will be taken." The Akkuyu project, costing more than $20 billion, is financed by Russia. Rosatom, its sole owner, can sell up to a 49% stake to a partner to share the investment burden. In April, Rosatom [USN:L6N4140Z0 TEXT:"said"] it started new talks with Turkish companies on joint ownership of Akkuyu after the Iran war spurred interest in such assets.

item.title: Kenya reports third Ebola case, a close relative of first two patients
item.description: Kenya reported its third Ebola infection on Friday, in a woman it said was closely related to the first two patients.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Kenya reported its third Ebola infection on Friday, in a woman it said was closely related to the first two patients. The 65-year-old had been in quarantine since October 6, the health ministry said in a statement. "Once she developed fever, sore throat and malaise, she was isolated and specimen collected for testing," it added. "She was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care improving her chances of recovery." Authorities say Kenya's cases are linked to the Ebola epidemic in Congo — the [USN:L8N45Z1AX TEXT:"second-largest"] outbreak ever recorded, with more than 9,000 cases and more than 4,000 deaths. Kenya's [USN:L8N45S0GY TEXT:"first recorded case"] was a man who had been ill in Congo for about a month, then travelled by road to Uganda and flew to Nairobi on October 3. That Kenyan man was driven to hospital by a relative and died on October 5. The health ministry said the second patient was in a stable condition and there was still no evidence the disease was spreading in the wider community. FEARS OF SCREENING LAPSES Ebola's spread to Kenya has raised concerns about lapses in screening systems. The first patient managed to cross the border between Congo and Uganda, which has been closed since May, and then pass through Nairobi's busy Jomo Kenyatta International Airport. Kenyan authorities say they have contacted 127 out of the 130 people known to have come into contact with the first patient. They had all been placed into quarantine and efforts were under way to trace the remaining three. Ebola spreads through direct contact with the bodily fluids of infected people, whether living or dead. The disease can cause fever, vomiting, diarrhoea and, in severe cases, internal and external bleeding. The outbreak in Congo was declared in mid-May but may have started months earlier. It is caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain, for which there are currently no approved vaccines or treatments. Uganda reported Ebola cases in May and June but was declared free of the virus in August. A doctor who returned to France in June from Congo tested positive but there have been no further cases there.

item.title: SpaceX's spectrum deal still leaves it far from rivaling telecom giants
item.description: SpaceX called its recent multibillion-dollar purchase of US airwaves a critical step towards building a mobile network, but constructing a true rival to major American carriers will require a terrestrial network and likely years of work and billions more.
item.dc:creator: Harshita Varghese
item.content:encoded: SpaceX called its recent multibillion-dollar purchase of US airwaves a critical step towards building a mobile network, but constructing a true rival to major American carriers will require a terrestrial network and likely years of work and billions more. Starlink became a money maker by offering internet service in rural and sparsely populated areas, where it faced little competition, as well as changing to easy-to-set-up home packages at a competitive price. Mobile will be harder. Cities are particularly tough places for mobile telephony and are technologically challenging for mobile-to-satellite connections. The rocket and satellite company will likely need to invest heavily in ground infrastructure, customer service, handset subsidies and promotions — costly parts of the wireless business in which AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile already have extensive operations. Building a network would cost more than $80 billion, according to TD Cowen, and add to SpaceX's capital demands as it pours money into its Starship rocket program, AI infrastructure, and Terafab chip factory. "It's just hard to imagine that this is all going to get done within a decade," said Julie Zhu, a research analyst at MoffettNathanson. "In the decade or so leading up to 2023, the big three spent about $650 billion in capex to build in networks that ostensibly were already finished." Most phones have small antennas and limited transmitting power that make reliable satellite connections more challenging because satellites orbit hundreds of kilometers above Earth, much farther away than cell towers. "There are too many pitfalls for satellite to be the only source of data," said Anshel Sag, principal analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy. SPACEX PUBLISHES HYBRID SPACE-TERRESTRIAL PLAN SpaceX has called the latest deal, in which [USN:L4N45U1O2 TEXT:"it acquired 800 MHz spectrum licenses from Grain"] at a price a source pegged at nearly $8 billion, a "critical next step" for the nascent Starlink Mobile to provide high-speed mobile service. "Starlink Mobile will deploy a flexible architecture combining our satellite-to-mobile constellation in space with an advanced terrestrial deployment that can seamlessly connect devices everywhere," including "indoors, outdoors, in cellular dead zones, and everywhere in between", SpaceX said, announcing the purchase. SpaceX has received regulatory authorization for up to 15,000 Starlink Mobile satellites and plans to deploy traditional terrestrial infrastructure such as antennas on towers and rooftops — a hybrid approach rather than pure satellite-to-phone — it laid out in a regulatory filing made public last week. In a Starlink Mobile system, satellites could connect directly to mobile phones and indirectly by relaying signals through ground infrastructure. This is similar to the technology of a partnership between Starlink and T-Mobile, which provides the terrestrial network while Starlink supplies the satellite connectivity that fills in where there are no towers. That is a T-Mobile-branded service. SpaceX in theory could strike a deal with one of the big three companies to use its ground infrastructure, what is known as a mobile virtual network operator, or MVNO, arrangement. However, SpaceX "appear to be going after a more build-your-own approach to a terrestrial network since nobody will offer them wholesale MVNO," Sag said. SpaceX would need several times more spectrum to match the holdings of the three big mobile companies, although current spectrum might be enough to start. "It is for a company with zero mobile subscribers, plenty of runway, and a robust device/equipment ecosystem," TD Cowen said. Would-be rivals dismissed the idea that the effort was an imminent threat. T-Mobile Chief Technology Officer John Saw said SpaceX's spectrum would not be enough to match the capacity and performance of established mobile networks, while Katie Magnotta, Verizon's associate vice president of corporate communications, said, "A company can have billions of dollars of spectrum, but if they do not have the network to use it, it's just empty airwaves."
