item.title: El S&P 500 opera con leve baja, subidas de bancos contrarrestan el nerviosismo por la IA
item.description: El índice de referencia S&P 500 cotizaba con una leve baja el viernes, ya que la preocupación por el sector de la inteligencia artificial ejercía presión sobre las acciones de los semiconductores, pero una subida de los bancos limitaba las caídas generales.
item.dc:creator: Tharuniyaa Lakshmi, Purvi Agarwal
item.content:encoded: El índice de referencia S&P 500 cotizaba con una leve baja el viernes, ya que la preocupación por el sector de la inteligencia artificial ejercía presión sobre las acciones de los semiconductores, pero una subida de los bancos limitaba las caídas generales. El sector de tecnología de la información del S&P 500 (.SPLRCT) era el que más golpeaba al índice, con una caída del 0,9%. CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , respaldada por Nvidia, perdía un 7,6% debido a la persistente preocupación por el endeudamiento del operador de centros de datos. Sus bonos sufrieron una fuerte venta masiva esta semana, lo que elevó sus rendimientos sobre el 15%. * Otras empresas de "neocloud", como Nebius Group (NBIS.O) e Iren (IREN.O) , caían más de un 5,5% cada una. * El sector de los semiconductores volvía a perder terreno: Micron Technology (MU.O) bajaba un 3,9% y Advanced Micro Devices (.AMD) , un 3,3%. El índice general de chips (.SOX) perdía un 1,8%, lo que lo sitúa ante la mayor caída porcentual en ocho sesiones desde la ola de ventas del "Día de la Liberación" en abril de 2025. La mayoría de las acciones de gran capitalización también registraban caídas: Alphabet (GOOGL.O) y Meta (META.O) cedían un 1%, lo que presionaba al sector de servicios de comunicaciones (.SPLRCL) y al Nasdaq. El retroceso de las acciones de chips de memoria a principios de esta semana, debido al temor por la competencia china y a la preocupación por la deuda de CoreWeave, "proporcionó a los inversores una excusa para reducir su exposición a todas las empresas relacionadas con la IA", dijo David Morrison, analista senior de mercados de Trade Nation. A las 15:19 GMT, el índice S&P 500 (.SPX) perdía 22,23 puntos, o un 0,29%, a 7.721,83 unidades, mientras que el Nasdaq (.IXIC) bajaba 292,66 puntos, o un 1,10%, a 26.420,37 unidades. En tanto, el Promedio Industrial Dow Jones (.DJI) sumaba 176,81 puntos, o un 0,34%, a 52.354,50 unidades. Por el contrario, la mayoría de los demás sectores del S&P 500 subían. El de materiales (.SPLRCM) era el que registraba la mayor alza porcentual, de un 1,6%, mientras que el sector financiero (.SPSY) ganaba un 1,1%. Las subidas de Goldman Sachs (GS.N) y JPMorgan Chase (JPM.N) impulsaban al Dow a su nivel más alto en más de un mes. El S&P 500 y el Nasdaq se encaminaban a registrar pérdidas semanales, ya que la caída provocada por la inteligencia artificial, los resultados bancarios dispares y los datos de inflación mermaron la confianza a lo largo de la semana. El Dow, por su parte, se encaminaba a cerrar la semana al alza. Los informes de esta semana sobre la inflación de los precios al consumo y al productor, más altos de lo esperado, han confirmado que las presiones sobre los precios se están traspasando desde la energía a otros productos.

item.title: Ryazan refinery halted processing at one primary unit after drone attacks, sources say
item.description: Russia's Ryazan oil refinery has suspended operations at one of its primary crude distillation units following a drone attack in the region on Thursday, two industry sources told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russia's Ryazan oil refinery has suspended operations at one of its primary crude distillation units following a drone attack in the region on Thursday, two industry sources told Reuters. A big Ukrainian drone attack on Russia's Ryazan region caused a fire to break out at an oil refinery, the regional governor Pavel Malkov said on [USN:L8N4610DI TEXT:"Thursday"]. The sources said on Friday that one of the oil refinery's main units, CDU-6, was halted following the attack. The unit had previously been suspended after another attack [USN:L8N4520GP TEXT:"last month"]. During the latest attack several refinery pipelines were also damaged. The refinery has another three primary crude distillation units - CDU-1, CDU-3 and CDU-4 - which continue to operate and may be used during the CDU-6 outage, according to the sources. Rosneft (ROSN.MM) , which owns the refinery, did not reply to a request for comment about the attack on the plant. The Ryazan oil refinery, which feeds Moscow with fuel, has been attacked several times this year. The plant has a processing capacity of 17 million metric tons per year, or some 340,000 barrels per day. The refinery can produce 3.4 million tons of gasoline and 3.8 million tons of diesel per year.

item.title: Colts release veteran WR Darius Slayton
item.description: The Indianapolis Colts have pulled the plug on the Darius Slayton experiment after less than a month.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Indianapolis Colts have pulled the plug on the Darius Slayton experiment after less than a month. The Colts signed the veteran wide receiver on Sept. 22 and released him on Friday without ever putting him on the field. Slayton, 29, was brought in for depth after the injury to Alec Pierce (heel) and due to his familiarity with quarterback Daniel Jones. Slayton reportedly struggled to pick up the offense in Indianapolis and was further hampered by a knee injury. He played for the New York Giants from 2019-25, catching 296 passes for 4,435 yards and 22 touchdowns in 106 games (78 starts). --Field Level Media

item.title: COP31 Les tortues caouannes, sentinelles du réchauffement en Méditerranée
item.description: Sous un ciel baigné de lune, des bébés tortues sortent du sable sur la côte méditerranéenne turque et se hâtent vers la mer, dans un cycle naturel ancestral de plus en plus menacé par le changement climatique.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Sous un ciel baigné de lune, des bébés tortues sortent du sable sur la côte méditerranéenne turque et se hâtent vers la mer, dans un cycle naturel ancestral de plus en plus menacé par le changement climatique. Tout au long de la nuit, le biologiste marin Yakup Kaska et son équipe de bénévoles veillent sur les nids. Des cages pyramidales protègent les œufs enfouis dans le sable contre les renards qui parcourent les quatre kilomètres de la plage d’Iztuzu: une plage touristique le jour, un sanctuaire pour la conservation des tortues la nuit. La tortue caouanne, qui pond sur les rivages de Méditerranée, est la mascotte de la COP31, la 31e conférence de l'Onu sur les changements climatiques que la Turquie accueillera du 9 au 20 novembre. La protection des écosystèmes marins figurera parmi les priorités de ce sommet organisé sur la côte, à Antalya. LA TORTUE MARINE, BAROMÈTRE DU CLIMAT "Les tortues marines nous fournissent un système d'alerte très rapide", explique Ayfer Sirin, maître de conférences en écologie à l’université d’Uskudar, qui a mené des recherches approfondies sur les tortues caouannes. Selon elle, à la croisée de la terre et de la mer, ces animaux sont les témoins des bouleversements qui gagnent les écosystèmes côtiers et marins. La température d’incubation détermine le sexe des nouveau-nés, les sables plus chauds favorisant la naissance de femelles. Une étude doctorale de cinq ans menée à l’université de Pamukkale par Ayfer Sirin a mis en évidence un lien entre le réchauffement, une ponte plus précoce, une incubation plus courte et une proportion de femelles atteignant 70% parmi les nouveau-nés de la plage de Patara. À Iztuzu, la température des nids a augmenté de près d'un degré Celsius en vingt ans, indique Yakup Kaska, ajoutant qu’une analyse plus large suggère que les femelles représentaient jusqu’à 80 à 90% des nouveau-nés dans de nombreuses populations de tortues marines. À mesure que le sable se réchauffe, l’équilibre entre les sexes se fragilise. Si les mâles deviennent trop rares, la reproduction pourrait être compromise. Au-delà de 30°C, la chaleur accroît également le risque de mortalité des embryons, souligne Ayfer Sirin. Les tortues caouannes sont classées comme "vulnérables" à l’échelle mondiale. Les populations méditerranéennes sont considérées comme de "préoccupation mineure", grâce aux progrès de la conservation, mais subissent de nouvelles pressions climatiques. HABITATS TRANSFRONTALIERS Yakup Kaska souligne que les migrations des tortues illustrent la nécessité d’une coopération transfrontalière, car elles nichent parfois en Turquie et se nourrissent en Tunisie ou dans l’Adriatique. Raison de plus pour appeler les pays à unir leurs efforts afin de protéger la biodiversité méditerranéenne. Le président de la COP31, Murat Kurum, ministre turc de l’Environnement, est allé dans ce sens lors d’une conférence sur les océans et les mers le mois dernier: "La protection des océans est une responsabilité que nous partageons tous. Nous appelons chaque partie à traduire cette responsabilité en actions audacieuses et concrètes: restaurer les écosystèmes et renforcer la résilience." DES FILETS DE PÊCHE AUX DÉCHETS PLASTIQUES Les caouannes femelles reviennent généralement pondre, des décennies plus tard, sur la plage où elles sont nées. Mais certaines gagnent désormais des côtes plus au nord, où elles étaient autrefois rares, observe Yakup Kaska. Iztuzu demeure un refuge essentiel: chaque saison, quelque 30.000 nouveau-nés émergent de centaines de nids et s’élancent vers la mer. Dans les flots, les nouveau-nés affrontent de nouveaux dangers: filets de pêche, bateaux et déchets plastiques. À quelques pas de la plage d’Iztuzu, le centre Dekamer offre un refuge aux tortues blessées, soignées dans de grands bassins, notamment après avoir été heurtées par des hélices de bateaux. Selon Yakup Kaska, 60% des tortues accueillies au centre ont au moins cinq morceaux de plastique dans leur système digestif. "Jeter un sac en plastique à la mer, c’est comme tirer une balle sur les tortues."

item.title: KFC switch to Coke puts PepsiCo's food service ties in focus, analysts say
item.description: KFC's decision to switch from Pepsi sodas to Coca-Cola at its US restaurants could raise questions about PepsiCo's other longstanding food service partnerships, analysts said, even as they expect the financial hit to be manageable.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: KFC's decision to [USN:L4N46120T TEXT:"switch"] from Pepsi sodas to Coca-Cola (KO.N) at its US restaurants could raise questions about PepsiCo's (PEP.O) other longstanding food service partnerships, analysts said, even as they expect the financial hit to be manageable. The loss of KFC comes as PepsiCo grapples with sluggish demand and higher costs in North America, where a recovery in growth and margins is taking [USN:L6N45U0N9 TEXT:"longer than expected"] and has prompted the company to deepen cost cuts. BofA analysts estimate the loss of the KFC account represents about $500 million in annual sales, equivalent to roughly a 3% hit to Pepsi Beverages North America's concentrate sales, while boosting Coca-Cola's North America sales by about 2.5% Brokerage Jefferies says the bigger concern for PepsiCo is the "loss of brand interaction and public perception" rather than the immediate financial impact "A longstanding Pepsi customer switching raises questions whether other accounts that have been historically off-limits are now up for grabs," Jefferies analysts said "Investors see this (move) less as a seismic commercial loss for PepsiCo and more as the natural order of... (a brand) reasserting itself," says Richard Exon, founder and partner at Joint, an independent creative  agency

item.title: Data centers may benefit from massive rural utility loan, US official says
item.description: A record-breaking $3.3 billion loan from the U.S. Department of Agriculture to a power plant in Georgia's Monroe County could potentially benefit data centers in the state, the agency's head of rural development said in an interview with Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Leah Douglas
item.content:encoded: A record-breaking $3.3 billion loan from the U.S. Department of Agriculture to a power plant in Georgia's Monroe County could potentially benefit data centers in the state, the agency's head of rural development said in an interview with Reuters. The administration of President Donald Trump has [USN:L1N45K0VR TEXT:"supported"] the rapid expansion of data centers, despite their [USN:L6N42I0TN TEXT:"unpopularity "]with communities concerned about water use and utility costs. Democrats are attempting to capitalize on that [USN:L6N45916H TEXT:"discontent "]in November's [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"]. Glen Smith, the USDA's Under Secretary for Rural Development, said in the Thursday interview that he hopes to secure more funding for such projects. Here are more details: The USDA announced on Tuesday the loan to Oglethorpe Power Corporation, the largest ever given under the agency's Rural Utilities Service. Smith said the plant will serve 38 rural utility cooperatives and support growing industry in the state, including potentially data centers. Last year, Google purchased nearly 1,000 acres of land in Monroe County for a data center. Oglethorpe spokesperson Blair Romero said in an email, "This facility is not dedicated to serving a data center. The new facility will help our Member cooperatives meet growing electricity demand across their communities." Smith said he plans to meet with congressional appropriators next week and request more money for such loans. "We have almost $8.6 billion in requests, and we're only into our fiscal year one month," he said. Smith said rural areas can benefit from data centers, "but you have to have the infrastructure in place. and that's where rural utilies and rural development comes into play." Data centers are driving US electricity use to [USN:L6N42Q137 TEXT:"record highs "]and in some regions, demanding more power than grids can supply. The Trump administration has not sought to regulate data center construction, instead asking tech companies to [USN:L1N3ZR10I TEXT:"pledge"] not to pass on electricity costs to consumers.

item.title: Meta employees said Lula's accounts were hindered during Brazil election, Folha reports
item.description: Employees at Meta acknowledged in internal communications that the Instagram accounts of Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva were negatively affected by restrictions during the country's election, newspaper Folha de S.Paulo reported on Friday, citing messages it reviewed.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Employees at Meta (META.O) acknowledged in internal communications that the Instagram accounts of Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva were negatively affected by restrictions during the country's election, newspaper Folha de S.Paulo reported on Friday, citing messages it reviewed. The messages also acknowledged the platform recommended the profile of challenger Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, as well as his WhatsApp channel, according to the report. Meta did not immediately respond to a request for comment Lula will face Bolsonaro in a runoff on October 25, following a stronger-than-expected performance by the senator in the [USN:L6N45Q04L TEXT:"first-round vote"] earlier this month Lula's camp said earlier this week it would file a complaint before the Organization of American States alleging that Meta, which owns Instagram, WhatsApp and Facebook, manipulated social media during Brazil's election According to Lula's party, some of his posts appeared without a share button, suffered reduced reach, and had stories that prevented reactions and sharing, in addition to appearing without audio or playing at accelerated speed A justice at Brazil's top electoral court on Thursday ordered the company not to unjustifiably limit the reach of political content related to both candidates through the end of the runoff campaign The ruling also stipulated that Meta AI, the company's artificial intelligence chatbot, must not favor either candidate when generating election-related content

item.title: Chile's pension funds requested curbs on interest-rate bets before losses, Bloomberg reports
item.description: Executives at Chile's pension funds appealed to regulators for curbs on volatile interest-rate derivatives before a downturn in US Treasuries left them with billions of dollars in losses, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Executives at Chile's pension funds appealed to regulators for curbs on volatile interest-rate derivatives before a downturn in US Treasuries left them with billions of dollars in losses, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday. The report said that fund managers had flagged risks of positions that have since hit the system's most conservative fund hard. The losses have drawn criticism from some lawmakers and raised concerns among pensioners. Chile's [USN:L3N3OP1TQ TEXT:"private pension system"] is managed by firms known as Administradoras de Fondos de Pensiones (AFPs), or pension fund administrators, which oversee five investment funds ranging from Fund A, the riskiest, to Fund E, the most conservative. Earlier this week, the AFP Association's head of research, Roberto Fuentes Silva, attributed a decline in Fund E to rising US interest rates after Bloomberg reported that Chilean pension funds had posted losses of about $7.7 billion on interest-rate-related positions. Executives managing these pension funds had asked regulators in private conversations to enforce rules on the stockpiling of volatile derivatives, Bloomberg's Thursday report said, citing people familiar with the conversations. The lucrative nature of the trade meant the executives could not act independently without forgoing returns that rivals would continue to cash in, the report added. Chile's pension regulator did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment. Chilean lawmaker Nelson Venegas from the opposition Socialist Party described the AFP losses as "very serious," accusing pension fund managers of putting workers' savings at risk and calling for tougher measures against those responsible. Ximena Ossandón, a lawmaker from the right-leaning National Renewal party aligned with the [USN:L1N43N14S TEXT:"government"], said it was too early to draw conclusions and that authorities should first determine whether the AFPs had acted within existing regulations. “We should wait to determine whether the investments were made within the permitted framework or not," Ossandón said in a statement. The AFP Association has sought to reassure contributors, saying in a statement that pension fund performance should be assessed over the long term rather than based on short-term market fluctuations. "A pension fund does not have losses or gains; rather, it experiences increases or decreases in its valuation," Fuentes Silva told local media. Chile's current private pension system started in the early 1980s during the Augusto Pinochet dictatorship and relies solely on worker contributions managed by the AFPs. The system has long faced criticism for generating relatively low pensions while AFP operators continue to post significant profits. After years of political debate, Congress approved a major [USN:L3N3OP1TQ TEXT:"pension reform"] in January 2025, with the rollout beginning in stages from August last year and continuing over several years.

item.title: US FDA sets up board to oversee drug exclusivity determinations
item.description: The US FDA's drug evaluation department said on Friday it has formed a board to oversee and advise on exclusivity determinations made by the department, aiming to improve clarity and consistency of those decisions.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US FDA's drug evaluation department said on Friday it has formed a board to oversee and advise on exclusivity determinations made by the department, aiming to improve clarity and consistency of those decisions. Here are more details: FDA-granted exclusivity rewards innovation by giving newly approved drugs a period of market protection, before lower-cost generic competitors enter the market The CDER (Center for Drug Evaluation and Research) exclusivity board will oversee certain exclusivity determinations, including whether and what type of exclusivity should be granted and the appropriate scope of grants, the agency said on Friday The board will focus on 5-year new chemical entity exclusivity that is granted to a drug whose active ingredient has never before been approved by the FDA It will also oversee 3-year new clinical trial exclusivity grants that are meant for drugs that use a previously approved active ingredient, but their approval relies on new clinical studies conducted or funded by the sponsor It will advise on exclusivity for biological products too The board will not review other types of exclusivity apart from the three, it said The board also may evaluate and make recommendations regarding CDER's policies and practices relating to exclusivity and maintain records of exclusivity determinations

item.title: US federal bankruptcy court operations disrupted by cybersecurity incident
item.description: Several online services supporting US federal courts' bankruptcy systems have gone offline following a cybersecurity incident involving a court contractor, the Administrative Office of the US Courts (AOC) said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: A.J. Vicens
item.content:encoded: Several online services supporting US federal courts' bankruptcy systems have gone offline following a cybersecurity incident involving a court contractor, the Administrative Office of the US Courts (AOC) said on Thursday. BAE Systems Inc., a U.S. subsidiary of the British defense contractor BAE Systems (BAES.L) , operates the Bankruptcy Noticing Center's (BNC) systems and websites on behalf of the federal judiciary, the AOC said in a statement . BAE is "actively investigating this incident and working to restore operations," the AOC said in the statement. A BAE Systems spokesperson said on Friday that the company is "aware of a security incident that is isolated to the BNC system" and has taken immediate steps to address it. BAE Systems is "coordinating closely" with the courts on the response, the spokesperson said. All access to the BNC systems and websites BAE operates on behalf of the judiciary and the related bankruptcy noticing process is unavailable, the AOC said. The BNC "produces and transmits bankruptcy notices for all federal bankruptcy courts around the country," the AOC said. Affected websites include bnc.uscourts.gov, bankruptcynotices.uscourts.gov, notices.uscourts.gov as well as the National Creditor Registration Service. The incident also "halted the BNC's production and distribution of bankruptcy notices for bankruptcy courts," the AOC said. (This story has been corrected to fix the business name of BAE Systems Inc. and its description, in paragraph 2.)

item.title: CDC reports 4,410 measles cases as outbreak grows
item.description: The US CDC on Friday reported 4,410 measles cases nationwide as of October 15, an increase of 330 from its last update a week ago, as an outbreak of the highly contagious disease continues.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US CDC on Friday reported 4,410 measles cases nationwide as of October 15, an increase of 330 from its last update a week ago, as an outbreak of the highly contagious disease continues. Here are key details: Measles-related hospitalizations this year stand at 451, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said The state of Pennsylvania has reported five measles-related deaths The CDC has confirmed [USN:L4N45L13A TEXT:"two measles-associated deaths"] in 2026, though it has not identified the states involved Pennsylvania has reported 1,260 measles cases this year as of October 16, with 238 disease-related hospitalizations, according to state health department data Last month, the CDC [USN:L4N45A17G TEXT:"shifted"] to using mortality data from the National Center for Health Statistics for measles-related deaths, rather than relying on state health departments, a change that has drawn scrutiny The CDC [USN:L4N45Z1Q3 TEXT:"said"] on Tuesday it would deploy more support to Pennsylvania to help investigate the outbreak Children and teenagers aged 5 to 19 were the largest group affected by the disease at 1,856, or 42% of cases, followed by adults aged 20 and older at 1,787 cases, or 41%, CDC data showed Earlier this month, the state of New York [USN:L4N45R1BM TEXT:"declared"] a disaster emergency for the measles outbreak, the first such declaration by a US state

item.title: Zubimendi close to Arsenal return, Hincapie still sidelined, says Arteta
item.description: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said Martin Zubimendi could return for Sunday's Premier League match against Nottingham Forest, but Piero Hincapie is expected to remain sidelined after both players picked up injuries last week.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said Martin Zubimendi could return for Sunday's Premier League match against Nottingham Forest, but Piero Hincapie is expected to remain sidelined after both players picked up injuries last week. The duo suffered ankle injuries during a training session following Arsenal's 2-1 win over Leeds United and were ruled out of Tuesday's Champions League victory over Lille “Piero (Hincapie) is evolving really well... I am sure it's not going to take long, but he will probably need another week or two," Arteta told reporters on Friday “Zubimendi looks much better... We have another session tomorrow, and after that we will assess whether he's available to play against Forest” Arsenal will also be without Christos Tzolis, who is recovering from a muscle injury sustained on international duty, and William Saliba, who remains sidelined with a back problem

item.title: Putin envoy says Russia and US are discussing joint deals including on data centres
item.description: Russia and the US are discussing a range of new joint projects including nuclear-powered data centres in the wake of last week's agreement on diesel, President Vladimir Putin's investment envoy said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Soldatkin, Olesya Astakhova
item.content:encoded: Russia and the US are discussing a range of new joint projects including nuclear-powered data centres in the wake of last week's agreement on diesel, President Vladimir Putin's investment envoy said on Friday. Kirill Dmitriev said that US sanctions posed serious obstacles and criticised as "misguided" the Graham Act [USN:L1N45A0ZU TEXT:"signed by US President Donald Trump"] last month that aims to squeeze Russia's energy revenues through sanctions and tariffs. Nevertheless, he said the two countries were considering other forms of economic cooperation in the wake of the diesel deal. "We are also discussing joint projects in the field of Russian and US data centres, including with the use of small-scale nuclear power plants," he added, without giving details. Ukraine has this month attacked data centres of Russian tech group Yandex and banking and technology group Sberbank in what it called a response to Russian strikes on its own sites. Dmitriev, a key figure in Russia-US talks on ending the Ukraine war, has long been pushing for a range of ambitious potential deals including on minerals and energy. The Kremlin has expressed frustration that the US until now has linked any such agreements to a peace deal, which remains elusive. But Dmitriev expressed optimism that this was changing. "Naturally, progress is quite difficult; there is resistance - widespread resistance, in fact - from various quarters. Yet, as the example regarding diesel demonstrates, I believe we will soon be announcing several other significant initiatives. The ice has, in fact, begun to break," he told the Russian Energy Week conference in Moscow. "We are effectively implementing projects with the United States of America at this very moment, and we will continue to do so until the special military operation comes to an end," he added, using the Kremlin's term for the war. Dmitriev said the US Treasury had asked Russia's sovereign wealth fund, which he heads, to help sort out tricky payment issues relating to the diesel agreement. The [USN:L8N4610WB TEXT:"deal"] announced by Trump a week ago involves the supply of Russian diesel to US and global markets in order to lower the price of the fuel, a key priority for the US president ahead of next month's mid-term elections. Fiercely [USN:L1N46209U TEXT:"criticised"] by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, it requires the removal of some sanctions on Russian oil that Trump himself has imposed. "There are so many layers of sanctions piled on top of one another that everyone has become confused; it's difficult now to figure out how to navigate a way out of this situation," Dmitriev told the Moscow conference. "Brainstorming sessions are already under way regarding how to lift these sanctions - that is exactly what the United States is currently working on." He said his Russian Direct Investment Fund "will work to ensure that all payments are efficient and reach their intended recipients".

item.title: Dodge the cops, reach the protest: India's latest online political game goes viral
item.description: A web-based multiplayer game in which players dodge police and detention on their way to a protest site in New Delhi has gone viral, as young Indians use satire and humour to respond to police actions.
item.dc:creator: Tora Agarwala, Aftab Ahmed
item.content:encoded: A web-based multiplayer game in which players dodge police and detention on their way to a protest site in New Delhi has gone viral, as young Indians use satire and humour to respond to police actions. As [USN:L6N46206J TEXT:"youth-led protests"] over [USN:L4N3TC0XX TEXT:"jobs"], [USN:L4N43O0C9 TEXT:"exam paper leaks"] and [USN:L4N45K0E7 TEXT:"voter roll revisions"] spread across India, a growing crop of online games is transforming political grievances into shareable digital content. The trend shows a generation raised on Instagram is expressing dissent in ways that differ sharply from the political communication style of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. One such game, 'Jantar Mantar Chalo', was developed by 27-year-old IT professional Suraj Kushwah, who has described it as "dark humour". The game satirises the difficulties protesters face in reaching Jantar Mantar, a main protest site in the capital, amid police blockades, road closures and public transport suspensions. Players can build a kafila, or procession, evade checkpoints and stage a demonstration, or switch sides and deploy batons and tear gas to disperse crowds. "Whatever news was coming was kind of like a circus," Kushwah said. "People were trying to reach Jantar Mantar. And they were getting detained. And I imagined it as a 3D game." Kushwah said at least 2,000 people had been playing the game at any point in time since its release on October 14. Another game casts firebrand left-wing activist [USN:L4N45X011 TEXT:"Neha Bora"] as the protagonist of a retro 8-bit-style platform reminiscent of classic arcade games. "We as artists believe that satire is the most powerful way to talk about things," said 30-year-old Anav Nayar, who co-developed the game with his brother, Akshay. The protests were triggered by the "[USN:L1N43O05A TEXT:"cockroach""] youth movement, which also started as a joke online. The games draw inspiration from protests against the Election Commission's voter roll revision exercise, which opposition parties and activists say has disenfranchised 130 million eligible voters and favoured Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party. The Election Commission and BJP deny the allegations. Gen Z's style of expression poses an unusual challenge for Modi. After the "cockroach" movement forced the resignation of Modi's education minister in July, he intensified outreach to younger Indians through self-shot Instagram videos. But analysts say Modi's outreach might not be enough. "The BJP has long enough enjoyed its dominance of controlling the narrative online and on the ground, but this time the younger generation has countered them everywhere," said Rasheed Kidwai, a political analyst.

item.title: US solicits exchange of up to 17 million barrels of oil from strategic reserve
item.description: The United States has issued a request for proposal for an exchange of up to 17 million barrels of crude oil from the nation's Strategic Petroleum Reserve, the Department of Energy said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The United States has issued a request for proposal for an exchange of up to 17 million barrels of crude oil from the nation's Strategic Petroleum Reserve, the Department of Energy said on Friday. The exchange would be part of a global deal the US struck [USN:FWN3ZY1GJ TEXT:"in March"] to try to control fuel prices impacted by the war on Iran. Washington agreed then to loan 172 million barrels of oil from the SPR as part of a wider deal with about 30 countries in the International Energy Agency to release 400 million barrels from reserves around the world. The US had previously offered to loan the last batch from the March deal in June. But the US revealed later that month that companies, required to pay premiums of up to 24% in the form of extra barrels of crude returned to the SPR, [USN:L1N42U0WE TEXT:"only agreed to borrow about 500,000"] barrels.

item.title: Starlink disruptions are being felt on the front lines of Ukraine
item.description: For one artillery unit fighting in eastern Ukraine, the US decision this week to reduce services provided by satellite company Starlink to the military had an immediate impact.
item.dc:creator: Sergiy Chalyi
item.content:encoded: For one artillery unit fighting in eastern Ukraine, the US [USN:L1N4610ZC TEXT:"decision"] this week to reduce services provided by satellite company Starlink to the military had an immediate impact. Communications with headquarters were interrupted and internet speeds dropped, posing risks in a war where drones present a constant danger and up-to-date information on targets and threats can make the difference between life and death. "Immediately after the announcement that the connection with Starlink was deteriorating, it really did have a negative impact," said Ukrlan, a 28-year-old serving with an artillery unit of the Special Rifle Police Battalion. He asked to be identified only by his callsign, in keeping with Ukrainian military practice. "We felt it straight away," he told Reuters from his bunker near the front line in the fiercely contested region of Donbas. "The internet speed at our position had deteriorated significantly and communication with our headquarters and our command had deteriorated significantly." According to officials, the White House issued an order to limit SpaceX's Starshield satellite system used by Ukraine for battlefield communications and drone operations. A US official has denied that President Donald Trump ordered a deliberate slowdown of Starshield, and Trump said this week intelligence sharing with Ukraine continued. Ukraine and its Western partners [USN:L1N46209U TEXT:"decried"] the slowdown as aiding Russia in the war, which began nearly five years ago with Moscow's full-scale invasion . The US says it wants to end the war and is working towards doing so. While much of the focus has been on Starshield, the military-grade version of SpaceX's Starlink service, Ukrlan's comments point to broader disruptions affecting internet connectivity and speeds. ROAR OF THE GUN Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy [USN:S8N4390AY TEXT:"told leaders"] in Brussels on Friday that Starlink services had improved but had not yet been fully restored, which he said put civilian lives at risk. "Starlink is really necessary for Ukraine. And unfortunately, in short term, Europe can't replace this capability," said the EU's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas. Ukrlan's unit had been firing a howitzer at Russian targets from a heavily camouflaged position dug deep into the ground. Soldiers hurriedly prepared shells in a dark, timber-framed bunker by the light of head torches, covering their ears each time the gun roared and filled the space with smoke. Ukrainian soldiers have said slower Starlink speeds have impaired the military's ability to detect and intercept incoming missiles and drones. The US move to temporarily restrict the system came as President Donald Trump has pressured Kyiv to stop its attacks on Russian oil refineries. He has blamed those strikes for soaring energy prices that are denting his Republican Party's prospects in the November midterm elections , although experts say that the spike is mainly the result of the US war with Iran. For Ukrainians, the consequences of his approach are clear. "At first he insisted very strongly that he would help us bring it to an end in a very short space of time," Ukrlan said, referring to Trump's promise to end the Ukraine war soon after his return to office. "But we haven't seen any sign of that at all. And things are just getting worse every day, every week."

item.title: AkzoNobel, Axalta offer remedies in bid for EU approval for $25 billion deal
item.description: Dulux paint maker AkzoNobel and US peer Axalta Coating Systems have offered remedies in an effort to secure EU antitrust approval for their $25 billion merger, a European Commission filing showed on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Yun Chee Foo
item.content:encoded: Dulux paint maker AkzoNobel (AKZO.AS) and US peer Axalta Coating Systems (AXTA.N) have offered remedies in an effort to secure EU antitrust approval for their $25 billion merger, a European Commission filing showed on Friday. The companies put in their offer on Thursday, automatically triggering a 10 working day extension of the Commission's deadline to November. The EU competition enforcer did not provide details of the concessions in line with its policy. The companies [USN:L1N45U0UA TEXT:"will offer to sell AkzoNobel's vehicle refinish business"] to address competition concerns and expect to secure EU clearance at the end of the preliminary review, sources told Reuters last week. The Commission is expected to seek feedback from rivals and customers before deciding whether to give the deal the green light, demand more or open a full-scale investigation. Axalta exclusively makes coatings, with a strong presence in the US market. BASF's (BASFn.DE) coatings business, Nippon Paint (4612.T) , Sherwin-Williams (SHW.N) and Kansai Nerolac (KANE.NS) compete with AkzoNobel and Axalta.

item.title: 3 goals of cybersecurity help you achieve a fourth
item.description: John Bandler of Bandler Law Firm PLLC outlines three sets of principles, or "triads," to help organizations understand and improve their cybersecurity program and achieve peace of mind.
item.dc:creator: John Bandler
item.content:encoded: John Bandler of Bandler Law Firm PLLC outlines three sets of principles, or "triads," to help organizations understand and improve their cybersecurity program and achieve peace of mind. This column features a trio of triads. First are cybersecurity goals, which will help you understand and prioritize cybersecurity to improve your law firm or organization. These three goals will help you achieve an important fourth goal, which can even improve your mental state. Knowing the next two triads helps you intelligently discuss cybersecurity principles with your technical and cybersecurity providers and experts, and to better understand cybersecurity laws and frameworks. Consider these three goals of cybersecurity for your organization: (1) Protect from cybercrime or other serious mishaps, (2) Comply with legal requirements, and (3) Fulfill the mission, including by improving efficiency and the management of information systems. We introduced these goals in an earlier column (see, "Maintain and improve the cybersecurity program of your firm or organization", Reuters Legal News, Feb 17, 2026, https://bit.ly/3U1FjJ8) and will discuss further in a moment. The Venn diagram from that article showed a bubble for each goal with some areas overlapping and others distinct. Now we can add to that diagram and introduce the fourth goal, peace-of-mind, which encircles all three. When organizations work honestly and effectively to achieve the three goals, while doing their reasonable best, that provides peace-of-mind. This is not a guarantee of imperviousness or success, but as much assurance and certainty as life and business can provide. In contrast, when organizations ignore the three goals and neglect to work on their cybersecurity program, no such comfort can be achieved. Leaders are left with nagging worries in the pit of their stomach because important actions remain undone and the chances of damage are heightened. If they fall victim to cybercrime, they may be accused of being negligent and sloppy, and it will be harder to defend against that claim. Let's briefly consider what each of the three goals entails. The goal of protect puts focus on preventing the bad things that could happen, including attacks by cybercriminals (data breach, ransomware, email-based frauds and thefts) and also system outages. Protect is focused on traditional risk analysis; thinking about the harms that could occur, then deciding what to do about them — if anything. Often, this means taking steps to prevent them from happening in the first place, or reducing the damage that might result. Comply focuses on the legal and professional duties of cybersecurity, and every organization has legal requirements there. At the most basic level, think of simple negligence, and how organizations should expend reasonable and diligent efforts to achieve reasonable cybersecurity. No firm leader would ever say, "We are content to take the negligent and sloppy approach to cybersecurity." Faced with such a claim by an outsider, they would defend and contest it, and attempt to show facts to demonstrate their cybersecurity was reasonable. Don't wait for a cybercrime or such a claim to start thinking about your cybersecurity, take the steps now to ensure you can defend against such a claim later. By doing so, you will also reduce the chance of ever being subjected to it. Attorneys have specific professional duties relating to cybersecurity and to protect client confidences and funds. Attorneys are lucrative cybercrime targets because they are involved directly and indirectly in a multitude of financial transactions and payments. Cybercriminals work to breach email accounts and redirect the transfers of funds to steal those payments. All states impose legal requirements for data breach notification, and many states have cybersecurity requirements. Other laws and regulations may apply, depending on the sector. In sum, every attorney, law firm, and organization has legal requirements relating to cybersecurity, and attorneys have professional ethical duties. Compliance with those rules protects and gives peace of mind. Focus upon the goal of mission allows us to examine all the things that can go right when law firms, lawyers, and others properly manage their information assets. They can efficiently access email, contacts, and documents, spending more time doing work, life, and pleasure, and less time struggling with (or cursing at) IT systems. In many ways mission comes first because no organization exists just to comply with rules, nor just to protect from cybercrimes. Law firms exist to serve clients (often this means bringing in revenue too) and every organization has a mission. This "CIA" triad is a cybersecurity basic principle that is less intuitive but good to know since cybersecurity laws, frameworks, and professionals mention it. If you hadn't heard about the CIA triad before, now you can nod knowingly when you read or hear it next. The three objectives of cybersecurity are: •Confidentiality •Integrity, and •Availability. Confidentiality means keeping unauthorized users from accessing the systems or data. Passwords, two-factor authentication, and hundreds of other measures help keep our data and systems confidential and safe. When a cybercriminal breaks into a law firm's email systems and documents, confidentiality has been violated. Integrity means that only authorized users can make changes in your system. When a cybercriminal uses a lawyer's email systems to send an email which misdirects a bank wire, integrity has been violated. Availability means that authorized users can access their systems and data when needed. Ransomware and other cybercrimes can remove the availability of data and systems. In order to achieve the three objectives or three goals, organizations (and individuals) can apply appropriate cybersecurity controls, which are also known as cybersecurity safeguards. Think of these as more discrete tasks or steps along the way to a broader objective. Cybersecurity laws and frameworks incorporate this concept as well. There are different ways to categorize these controls but an important way is with the initialism of "PAT," which stands for •Physical •Administrative, and •Technical. Physical controls restrict physical access in one way or another. Locking a door, a receptionist who controls access, securing your phone or purse while in a public place are all examples of physical controls. Administrative controls include rules, policies, procedures, and training. Your organization should have a cybersecurity policy and conduct cybersecurity training. Technical controls are electronic protections, such as a firewall, antivirus, or monitoring software. These three control types illustrate that cybersecurity is not just about the technical aspects, but many others too, including those that are in the lawyer's wheelhouse. A trio of triads. We begin with the one that is less well known but is intuitive and simple to help us understand why we do cybersecurity and what we can achieve. Do these sufficiently and we get the fourth goal of peace-of-mind, knowing we are doing our reasonable, diligent best with cybersecurity. Two are well-known and good to know, even though less intuitive to the casual observer. Cybersecurity professionals know them well and you will see their pattern imprinted upon many cybersecurity laws and best practices. None of these triads replace the broader process of building and improving your organization's cybersecurity program, as we covered in prior articles. They do help with continual improvement and refined understanding of your program. Fight the tendency for fear, uncertainty and doubt. Remember that for each step of improvement that you take with your organization's cybersecurity, you travel further away from the nagging worries of tasks and duties left undone, and closer towards your peace of mind with reasonable cybersecurity or better. John Bandler is a lawyer, consultant, author, and adjunct professor at Elisabeth Haub School of Law at Pace University. He helps protect organizations from cybercrime, improve cybersecurity and better protect and manage information systems. His latest book is "Cyberlaw: Law for Digital Spaces and Information Systems" (2025). His firm, based in New York, is Bandler Law Firm PLLC, and he can be reached at JohnBandler@JohnBandler.com.

item.title: Central bankers eye higher rates as AI boom fuels scramble for cash
item.description: The artificial intelligence boom is setting off a global race for money, forcing central bankers to contemplate a future in which interest rates stay higher and governments need to tighten their belts after an era of largesse.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Canepa, Leika Kihara, Rae Wee
item.content:encoded: The artificial intelligence [USN:L1N45C04W TEXT:"boom"] is setting off a global race for money, forcing central bankers to contemplate a future in which interest rates stay higher and governments need to tighten their belts after an era of largesse. From silicon chips and data centres to power grids and telecoms networks, governments and companies are pouring money into projects tied directly or indirectly to AI, adding fuel to the global economy and [USN:L1N45V0NY TEXT:"pushing up borrowing costs"]. Central bankers from the world's largest economies gathering in Bangkok said the boom was also creating fresh inflation pressures and financial risks, because the investment is arriving long before the productivity gains AI promises. "If you're a central banker...you've got to recognise this as a shock," Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh said at the [USN:L1N4620A6 TEXT:"annual meetings"] of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank in Bangkok. "It's obviously hitting the demand side of the economy before it's going to hit the supply side." Warsh, who said the US was benefiting from a broadening "surge of investment", warned the transition could be "very bumpy" as investors, companies and policymakers grappled with a technology whose ultimate winners remain unclear. Several of his colleagues from the G20 group of large economies also in the Thai capital said it would only take a slight reassessment of the rosy earnings prospects underpinning AI investments to cause profound market ructions, as a [USN:L1N461090 TEXT:"selloff in Asian tech stocks"] showed this week. STARS BEHIND THE CLOUDS The debate marks a striking shift from the years following the 2008 financial crisis, when policymakers worried about excess global savings and inflation that was persistently too low. Now central bankers increasingly see the opposite problem: too much demand for capital. "There is a global fight for money," ECB policymaker Martins Kazaks told Reuters. "Investment in AI is one of the key factors driving up the cost of money." That pressure is being amplified by governments from the United States to Japan and Germany borrowing heavily for defence, industrial policy and energy projects. For central bankers, the implication is that the level of interest rates needed to keep economies on an even keel, known as R-star, may be rising. "The problem at the moment in calculating the R-star is that the stars are covered by the clouds, and the clouds are so thick," South African Reserve Bank Governor Lesetja Kganyago said. "We know that R-star is higher, but we do not know how high." A higher neutral rate means the same level of interest rate is less restrictive than previously thought. "Maybe rates, on average, will be that little bit higher," said Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill. The Bank of Japan has already cited AI-related demand as a factor behind its recent rate increases, arguing that investment-driven price pressures have become broader and more persistent. Economists expect the Bank of England to raise rates at its next meeting on November 5. The ECB and Fed raised rates in September, and markets have priced in another move by them both in December. NO MORE CHEAP MONEY The prospect of structurally higher borrowing costs poses a challenge for governments that built up large debts during years when interest rates hovered near zero. Sovereign bond yields have [USN:L8N45N0KW TEXT:"risen across the world"], and in recent weeks some have reached levels not seen since before the global financial crisis. The euro zone, and notably [USN:L1N45N0CH TEXT:"debt-laden France"], was seen as particularly exposed. Much of the AI-driven investment surge is taking place in the United States and, to a lesser extent, Japan and other parts of Asia, with [USN:L6N4610HN TEXT:"ASML"] and Siemens among the few clear European winners. Meanwhile, the bloc faces higher energy costs from wars in Iran and Ukraine , compounding inflation pressures and squeezing public finances. "There are particular circumstances that lead to some countries being more affected, France being a case in point," ECB President Christine Lagarde said at a CNN event in Bangkok. "And for that one, the primary and first solution lies at home in France. And it has to do with fiscal policies."

item.title: Thousands march in Albanian capital as anti-government protests spread
item.description: Thousands of young Albanians marched through Tirana on Friday, breaking some windows and traffic lights on the fourth day of an increasingly violent student-led campaign to force Prime Minister Edi Rama to resign.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Thousands of young Albanians marched through Tirana on Friday, breaking some windows and traffic lights on the fourth day of an increasingly violent student-led campaign to force Prime Minister Edi Rama to resign. The demonstrations, which are spreading through the country, [USN:L1N4610AQ TEXT:"turned into a riot"] in the capital on Thursday, with protesters smashing windows, raiding a bank and clashing with police. They follow months of mostly peaceful demonstrations that the students say the government ignored. "They are pushing us to the limits," said 19-year-old protester Enea, declining to give a second name for fear of arrest. He said his message to Rama was: "To resign as fast as possible before everything burns down." The students accuse officials of corruption and neglecting education and say they are angry about the sale of pristine parts of Albania's coast to a luxury resort development backed by US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner. The unrest is a challenge for Rama, who won a fourth term last year on promises to take Albania into the European Union and is aiming for membership as early as 2028. "We will not bow to violence," he said on Facebook. BUSINESSES APPEAL TO PROTESTERS TO LEAVE THEM ALONE The students, many wearing masks, faced off against lines of riot police in front of the Education Ministry building. Some small businesses had their shutters down and notes on their facades saying: "We are with you. Do not damage our business all over the town." In the coastal town of Lezha, police clashed with stone-hurling protesters. Protests have also spread to Elbasan, Skhodra and Korca, where demonstrators broke windows and set fire to garbage bins, local media reported. "We've been protesting peacefully for 140 days, and nothing was heard. So this is our only chance to be heard and get our rights that we deserve," a 19-year-old protester who gave her name only as Klea said. The demonstrations were sparked by the plans to build the resort, which has faced legal challenges. Villagers told Reuters in July that their land was wrongfully sold for development. Reuters later reported that the man who sold the land was wanted by prosecutors for drug trafficking, charges his lawyer denied. Reuters found no evidence of wrongdoing by Kushner, who is not directly involved in the villagers' dispute. Political analyst Afrim Krasniqi said younger generations saw no future in Albania. "They see that all resources in the country, political resources, economic, everything is in the hands of oligarchs," he told Reuters. Corruption scandals have tarnised Albania's image over the years and analysts say the country is a hub for gangs seeking to launder money from drugs and weapons trafficking, complicating its efforts to join the EU. Along with Montenegro, Albania is leading the accession process among Balkan countries. The unrest is part of a wave of student activism in Europe. In France, high school students [USN:L1N45Z0DG TEXT:"have staged weeks of protests"] and school blockades demanding more teachers and better facilities, arguing that deteriorating school buildings and overcrowded classrooms are undermining education.

item.title: US import prices increase; post largest annual gain in more than four years
item.description: US import prices increased more than expected in September, boosted by higher costs for energy products and a range of other goods, further evidence of rising inflation pressures as the Middle East conflict persists.
item.dc:creator: Lucia Mutikani
item.content:encoded: US import prices increased more than expected in September, boosted by higher costs for energy products and a range of other goods, further evidence of rising inflation pressures as the Middle East conflict persists. The report from the Labor Department on Friday followed data this week showing strong increases in [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"consumer"] and [USN:L1N460127 TEXT:"producer"] prices last month, which left economists convinced that inflation was broadening beyond the energy sector. The drawn-out US-Israeli war with Iran has snarled supply chains, and is keeping oil prices elevated. Economists have attributed rising inflation to President Donald Trump's policies, including tariffs on imports and the Middle East conflict. A Reuters/Ipsos poll also showed about 78% of Americans [USN:L6N45T0W3 TEXT:"blamed Trump's"] policies for the rising cost of living. "Americans face an inflation threat literally on every front and everywhere they turn they have to reach in their pocketbooks and pay a little bit more for the same goods that were cheaper just a few months ago," said Christopher Rupkey, chief economist at FWDBONDS. "There was no import goods inflation before Trump 2.0 economic policies started to roll out in January 2025, but this year it is everywhere." Import prices jumped 1.1% last month after rebounding by a downwardly revised 0.5% in August, the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast import prices, which exclude tariffs, increasing 0.8% after a previously reported 0.7% advance in August. In the 12 months through September, import prices rose 8.1%, the largest gain since July 2022, after increasing 6.7% in August. Despite inflation heating up in September, financial markets still expected the Federal Reserve to skip raising interest rates later this month and tighten monetary policy in December. The US central bank in September raised its [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"overnight benchmark interest rate"] by 25 basis points to the 3.75%-4.00% range. Fed Chairman [USN:S0N40K04F TEXT:"Kevin Warsh,"] speaking in Bangkok, Thailand, on Friday gave no preview about whether he feels more interest-rate hikes will be needed, or when, in keeping with his style since taking the reins as central bank chief in May. Stocks on Wall Street were mixed. The dollar fell against a basket of currencies. US Treasury yields fell. Imported fuel prices rebounded 4.8% last month after falling 0.2% in August. Food prices were unchanged after dropping 0.6% in August. Excluding food and fuels, import prices advanced 0.7%, matching the prior month's increase. The so-called core import prices rose 6.2% in the 12 months through September. Capital goods prices increased 0.9% after rising by the same margin in August, boosted by prices for computers, peripherals and semiconductors amid an AI investment boom. There was also a rise in the cost of imported industrial and service machinery, which more than offset a decline in the prices of scientific and medical machinery. ACCELERATION IN INFLATION ANTICIPATED Prices for imported consumer goods, excluding automotives, increased 0.4%, driven by a 0.7% surge in the cost of long-lasting manufactured goods. The cost of imported automotive vehicles, parts and engines increased 0.3%. Prices of imports from China increased 0.7%, the most since December 2021. Prices gained 3.1% in the 12 months through September. There were also increases in the prices of imports from Japan, the European Union, Mexico and Canada. The report also showed a 12.6% surge in import air passenger fares last month after declining in July and August. Economists said the international airfares component that goes into the calculation of the Personal Consumption Expenditures price indexes, the inflation measures tracked by the Federal Reserve for its 2% target, was unchanged after they adjusted the data for seasonal fluctuations. Economists' estimates for the increase in September's core PCE price index were little changed in the 0.31% to 0.36% range, which could round up to 0.4%. That would translate to a year-over-year rise of 3.1%. Core PCE inflation gained 0.2% in August and advanced 3.0% on a year-over-year basis. "We're looking for inflation to accelerate in the near term but not plateau at a higher level," said Oren Klachkin, financial markets economist at Nationwide. "That said, the risk is inflation remains higher for longer than we expect and is more difficult for the Fed to vanquish." Though the AI investment spree is contributing to fueling inflation, it is also underpinning manufacturing. A separate report from the Fed showed [USN:L1N46110A TEXT:"factory production"] rebounded 0.3% in September, also supported by businesses replenishing inventories to meet robust domestic demand. Output fell 0.2% in August. It advanced 1.1% on a year-over-year basis in September. But factory production lost significant momentum in the third quarter, growing at a 0.7% annualized rate after accelerating at a 5.6% pace in the April-June quarter. Manufacturing accounts for about 9.4% of the economy. Output of semiconductors and related electronic components surged 28.4% last quarter, which some economists shrugged off. Motor vehicle and parts production fell 3.0% in September and contracted at a 3.4% rate last quarter. "While strong AI-demand has boosted business investment, much of this investment is imported, implying domestic production has not been as strong," said Veronica Clark, an economist at Citigroup. Outside AI-supporting industries, downside risks to production are mounting from elevated energy prices, a trade war with Canada, rising borrowing costs and fading stimulus from tax incentives. Record high diesel prices could soon raise the cost of goods, including at the supermarket, weighing on demand. Capacity utilization for the manufacturing sector edged up to 75.9% from 75.8% in August. It is 2.3 percentage points below its long-run average. "This means producers may be inclined to absorb some of the increase in energy and other input costs, but clearly not all, as suggested by this week's heated consumer and producer price reports," said Sal Guatieri, a senior economist at BMO Capital Markets.

item.title: Hedge funds bet Japan reforms have further to run at Sohn Tokyo
item.description: The next phase of Japanese corporate reform took center stage at the Sohn Conference in Tokyo, as hedge fund managers highlighted investment opportunities ranging from a financial conglomerate's capital allocation strategy to an X-ray scattering firm's AI solutions.
item.dc:creator: Summer Zhen, Rocky Swift
item.content:encoded: The next phase of Japanese corporate reform took center stage at the Sohn Conference in Tokyo, as hedge fund managers highlighted investment opportunities ranging from a financial conglomerate's capital allocation strategy to an X-ray scattering firm's AI solutions. At the inaugural Sohn Conference in Japan, which invited 14 funds to pitch their top investment ideas, more than half of the investors favored the theme of corporate reform. Daisuke Nakayama, a portfolio manager at Hong Kong-headquartered Polymer Capital, picked Orix Corporation , a financial services firm, saying the change in management marks "a big turning point" for the company's transformation into a global investment firm. "The new leadership has a greater focus on capital allocation and ROE," Nakayama said, adding the firm is now using overseas capital, including from Qatar Investment Authority, to bid for companies. The number of activist campaigns in Japan hit a record last year, according to brokerage Jefferies, after years of pressure from regulators and the Tokyo Stock Exchange on companies to improve shareholder returns and invest in growth. BEYOND DIVIDENDS AND BUYBACKS Fund managers said that the next chapter is not just about companies increasing dividends and buybacks but also about focusing on those deploying capital to expand businesses and drive long-term growth. One example is Rigaku (268A.T) , an X-ray equipment supplier pivoting to semiconductor metrology, measuring and inspecting chips. New York-based Indus Capital Partners said it had invested in the company and had engaged with the firm to sell a stake to a US semiconductor firm to drive revenue. As semiconductor companies are going into vertical structures to scale, X-ray is needed to detect defects deeper in the 3D chips, said Byron Gill, managing partner at Indus. Rigaku might be one of the few companies that "has the key to unlocking scale for the semiconductor industry in the middle of a super cycle", he added, forecasting a 100% rise in its valuation by 2029. REFORM THEME DOMINATES The corporate reform theme still has a long way to run, market participants said. "Japan changes slowly, but once the change starts, it does not reverse," said Naohide Une, partner and CEO at Investment Lab, a former senior managing director at Japan Post Bank. He picked Japanese chemical company Ube Corporation (4208.T) for its corporate reform efforts. In a separate Q&A session, Seth Fischer, founder of activist Oasis Management, said his fund may substantially increase its stake in Japanese electric motor maker Nidec (6594.T) . AI AS A BACK-OFFICE TAILWIND AI was another key investment theme. Investment firms Ruane Cunniff and Japan Catalyst picked software companies Money Forward (3994.T) and OBIC Business Consultants (4733.T) , respectively. They argued that back-office software operators are AI winners rather than losers, as clients require accuracy. And these businesses are helping Japan overcome labor tightness, they said.

item.title: Dólar se encamina a caída semanal por menor expectativa de alza de tasas de la Fed
item.description: El dólar bajaba el viernes, en camino a su primera caída semanal en más de un mes frente al euro y al yen, en medio de menores expectativas de un alza de tasas de interés de la Reserva Federal y preocupaciones por una ola de ventas en las bolsas impulsada por la inteligencia artificial.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Rebaudo, Laura Matthews
item.content:encoded: El dólar bajaba el viernes, en camino a su primera caída semanal en más de un mes frente al euro y al yen, en medio de menores expectativas de un alza de tasas de interés de la Reserva Federal y preocupaciones por una ola de ventas en las bolsas impulsada por la inteligencia artificial. * Los mercados se vieron sacudidos esta semana por datos de precios al consumo y a la producción más altos de lo esperado. * No obstante, las autoridades de la Fed aseguraron que no hay urgencia por endurecer la política monetaria, contribuyendo a estabilizar el rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro y minando el apoyo al dólar. * Las acciones del sector de la IA cayeron esta semana y la tensión se extendió a sectores del mercado crediticio, ya que los inversores a lo largo de toda la cadena de suministro temen ahora que los operadores de centros de datos no logren ser rentables a tiempo para pagar sus deudas. * "Desde mediados de junio, con un Comité Federal de Mercado Abierto de tono agresivo, las tasas han estado impulsando el dólar, y ahora parece que la preocupación sobre la sostenibilidad de la IA están contrarrestando ese efecto", dijo Marc Chandler, de Bannockburn Capital Markets. * El índice dólar , que compara al billete verde con una cesta de seis destacadas divisas, caía un 0,42% a 101,61 unidades, en camino a un descenso semanal del 0,6%. * La libra esterlina ganaba un 0,6%, a 1,3353 dólares, con un alza acumulada del 0,92% en la semana, mientras que el dólar restaba un 0,48% ante el franco suizo, al 0,8228%, lo que supone un declive semanal del 0,92%. * El euro subía un 0,33%, a 1,1255 dólares, tras mejorar un 0,56% el jueves, su mayor avance diario en dos meses y en camino a un alza semanal del 0,48%. Frente al yen, el dólar cedía un 0,12%, a 157,79 unidades, cerca de poner fin a cuatro semanas seguidas a la baja.

item.title: Shell agrees proposed sale of French fuel stations to DCC Energy, source says
item.description: Shell has agreed a deal with Dublin-based DCC Energy for the proposed sale of its network of fuel retail stations and related transport-fuels services in France, according to a person familiar with the matter and documents seen by Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Stephanie Kelly, Dimitri Rhodes
item.content:encoded: Shell (SHEL.L) has agreed a deal with Dublin-based DCC Energy for the proposed sale of its network of fuel retail stations and related transport-fuels services in France, according to a person familiar with the matter and documents seen by Reuters. The agreement comes as Shell aims to focus its fuel retail and charging operations on key markets where it generates the majority of its cash flow, including the US, Canada and the United Kingdom. The parties have yet to finalise the deal, although completion is expected in the second quarter of 2027, subject to consultation with employee representatives, the document showed. The transaction would include around 70 sites, eight LNG installations and the transfer of 35 employees, the document showed. "Shell is considering a sale of its retail forecourts business in France," Shell told Reuters, adding that it would not comment further at this stage. DCC Energy declined to comment. DCC Energy, a sales and distribution company in Europe and the US, serves millions of customers across the industrial and public sectors and delivers off-grid energy solutions, led by liquid gas, the company's website said. It also operates service stations and fleet services. DCC Energy would operate the stations under a long-term Shell brand licence, the document showed. However, Shell's core fuel supply operations are excluded, meaning the buyer would source its fuel independently. The monetary value of the deal could not immediately be determined. Shell's marketing unit, which includes its fuel and charging retail stations, reported $1.3 billion in adjusted earnings in the second quarter this year, compared with $1.2 billion during the same time last year.

item.title: Oro anota caída semanal mientras los operadores analizan las señales de la Fed
item.description: Los precios del oro se mantuvieron prácticamente estables el viernes pero anotaron una caída semanal mientras los operadores sopesaban la posibilidad de nuevas alzas de tasas de interés por parte de la Reserva Federal este año tras una serie de datos de inflación en Estados Unidos más altos de lo esperado.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Sinha
item.content:encoded: Los precios del oro se mantuvieron prácticamente estables el viernes pero anotaron una caída semanal mientras los operadores sopesaban la posibilidad de nuevas alzas de tasas de interés por parte de la Reserva Federal este año tras una serie de datos de inflación en Estados Unidos más altos de lo esperado. El oro al contado subió un 0,1% a 4.175,66 dólares por onza a las 1543 GMT, pero acumuló un descenso del 0,4% en la semana. Los futuros del oro estadounidense con entrega en diciembre subieron un 0,6% hasta los 4.196,40 dólares por onza. "Nos encontramos en un rango muy estrecho y nos inclinamos hacia el límite inferior de soporte, debido principalmente a que sigue habiendo mucha incertidumbre sobre lo que hará la Fed", afirmó Bart Melek, director global de estrategia de materias primas de TD Securities. El presidente de la Reserva Federal, Kevin Warsh, se mostró optimista sobre la solidez de la economía estadounidense, pero no dio pistas sobre la trayectoria de las tasas de interés del banco central. Los datos publicados el jueves revelaron que los precios al productor de Estados Unidos registraron el mes pasado su mayor subida en cuatro años y medio. Estos datos se sumaron al informe sobre los precios al consumo del miércoles, que mostraba una aceleración de los precios en septiembre. El presidente de la Fed de Chicago, Austan Goolsbee, calificó los datos de "desalentadores", mientras que la presidenta de la Fed de Cleveland, Beth Hammack, señaló que la Fed podría verse obligada a subir las tasas de interés de forma más agresiva si se produjera un deterioro notable de las expectativas de inflación del público. Los operadores esperan en su mayoría que el banco central estadounidense mantenga las tasas estables este mes, al tiempo que descuentan una probabilidad del 90% de que se produzca una subida de tasas en diciembre, según la herramienta FedWatch. Aunque el oro suele considerarse una cobertura contra la inflación, el aumento de las tasas de interés tiende a reducir el atractivo de este metal que no genera rendimiento. "Durante lo que queda de año, es probable que los precios del oro bajen ligeramente, a medida que la Fed siga subiendo las tasas y los temores en torno al fin del auge de la IA resulten ser temporales", afirmó Hamad Hussain, economista especializado en clima y materias primas de Capital Economics. Entre otros metales, la plata al contado se mantuvo estable en 57,43 dólares por onza, el platino subió un 0,6% a 1.636 dólares y el paladio bajó un 0,2% a 1.124,25 dólares. Los tres metales anotaron pérdidas semanales.

item.title: Swiss journalist risks court sentence for exposing top banker
item.description: Zurich prosecutors this week charged Swiss journalist Lukas Haessig with violating banking secrecy over reporting that set off a high-profile corporate criminal trial of the former boss of Raiffeisen Bank Switzerland, Haessig said on his financial blog Inside Paradeplatz.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Zurich prosecutors this week charged Swiss journalist Lukas Haessig with violating banking secrecy over reporting that set off a high-profile corporate criminal trial of the former boss of Raiffeisen Bank Switzerland, Haessig said on his financial blog Inside Paradeplatz. Zurich-based Inside Paradeplatz published a series of articles in 2016 about Pierin Vincenz, former CEO of Raiffeisen Bank Switzerland, and his business partner Beat Stocker, who were found guilty of fraud in April 2022 That verdict [USN:L8N4422LC TEXT:"is currently under review"] by a higher court expected to rule in January 2027 Police in June 2025 searched the blog's Zurich office and home of its founder, seizing evidence linked to suspected violation of Swiss banking law Prosecutors had dropped the case in December 2025, but Zurich's High Court in April said a court must decide how the banking secrecy provision should be interpreted after a complaint by Stocker Article 47 of the Swiss Banking Act criminalises disclosure of confidential information leaked by bank insiders, with penalties of up to three years in prison or a fine Press freedom group Reporters Without Borders Switzerland called the charges troubling and said Article 47 of the Swiss banking act must not be used to prosecute journalists Inside Paradeplatz's reporting was clearly in the public interest, Reporters Without Borders said, adding the banking secrecy law had a chilling effect and pointing to "legal shortcomings" in Switzerland on press freedom Prosecutors said the presumption of innocence applies to Haessig. No court date has yet been set

item.title: UK's FTSE 100 logs strongest week in six months on defensive-sector rally
item.description: Britain's blue-chip stocks had their best week in six months, as investors flocking to defensive sectors offset a rout in AI-linked stocks, while finance minister John Healey's reassurances on fiscal discipline also helped risk appetite.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's blue-chip stocks had their best week in six months, as investors flocking to defensive sectors offset a rout in AI-linked stocks, while finance minister John Healey's reassurances on fiscal discipline also helped risk appetite. The export-heavy FTSE 100 (.FTSE) closed 0.38% higher at 10,881.90 points, logging a weekly gain of 3.1%, the biggest since early April, while the midcap FTSE 250 (.FTMC) gained 0.45%. UK's large-cap ETFs attracted $3.38 billion in estimated net inflows year to date, already the biggest annual total since 2020, data from Morningstar showed "Flows into passive funds typically follow performance, but they also reflect investors looking to diversify away from US mega-cap technology and broaden their equity exposure," said Michael Born, an analyst at Morningstar Consumer staples supported gains. Cigarette maker British American Tobacco (BATS.L) rose 2.1%, while Johnnie Walker owner Diageo (DGE.L) gained 1.9% The beverages (.FTNMX451010) and medical equipment and services (.FTNMX201020) sectors advanced 7.8% and 6.9%, respectively, in the week Homebuilders (.FTNMX402020) jumped over 6% in the week after Healey [USN:S8N4040BJ TEXT:"reaffirmed"] his commitment to fiscal discipline on Thursday Banks (.FTNMX301010) were muted on Friday, recovering from early losses triggered by a [USN:SPN46001Q TEXT:"report"] that Healey was likely to tax the lenders in the budget Bank of England [USN:L1N46202H TEXT:"Governor Andrew Bailey"] said signs of second-round inflation were limited ahead of next week's inflation data Traders are pricing in four BoE rate hikes over the next 12 months, according to LSEG data Defence stocks (.FTNMX502010) extended a strong run on the day: BAE Systems (BAES.L) and Babcock International (BAB.L) rose 2.6% and 3.6%, respectively THG (THG.L) had its best week in six months, surging 30% after the e-commerce firm raised its annual adjusted core profit forecast on Thursday

item.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq set for steep weekly losses as AI jitters rattle investors
item.description: The benchmark S&P 500 and Nasdaq were set to end the week in the red, with technology stocks coming under more pressure on Friday over cracks in the AI trade and adding to losses.
item.dc:creator: Tharuniyaa Lakshmi, Purvi Agarwal
item.content:encoded: The benchmark S&P 500 and Nasdaq were set to end the week in the red, with technology stocks coming under more pressure on Friday over cracks in the AI trade and adding to losses. The S&P 500 information technology index (.SPLRCT) fell 1.5% and was the biggest drag. [USN:L6N4620IB TEXT:"Nvidia-backed"] CoreWeave (CRWV.O) slid 10.3% on lingering debt concerns. The data centre operator's bonds sold off sharply this week, pushing yields to above 15%. Semiconductors bore the brunt of the selloff, with the broader chips index (.SOX) dropping 1.8% — set for its steepest eight-session percentage decline since the "Liberation Day" selloff in April 2025. Most megacap stocks tumbled and brought the Nasdaq close to a one-month low. Meta (META.O) slipped 2.3% and Microsoft (MSFT.O) lost 1.8%. AI stocks have cratered this week over concerns that data centre operators might not turn profitable in time to repay debts, particularly with borrowing costs expected to rise. Worries over rising competition from China also dented sentiment. "When investors start worrying that AI names are overvalued, they gravitate toward lower-multiple stocks with stable cash flows," said Dennis Dick, founder and market structure analyst at Triple D Trading. Adding to concerns around AI financing, some current Anthropic investors and prospective investors [USN:L6N4611DN TEXT:"are weighing a lower valuation"] for the company in its upcoming IPO, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter. At 12:19 p.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) fell 14.74 points, or 0.03%, to 52,162.95, the S&P 500 (.SPX) lost 43.53 points, or 0.56%, to 7,700.38 and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) lost 348.31 points, or 1.30%, to 26,364.72.
