Most other S&P 500 sectors rose. The energy index (.SPNY) was the biggest percentage gainer, up 1.5%, while the financials index (.SPSY) rose 1%. Gains in Goldman Sachs (GS.N) and JPMorgan Chase (JPM.N) lifted the Dow to its highest level in over a month. The index is set for a weekly advance, with investors rushing to defensive sectors such as healthcare and consumer staples. "What we're seeing now is money rotating out of a very crowded AI trade and into value names," Dick added. The S&P 500 was set for its steepest weekly loss since early June, faced with an AI-led rout, mixed bank earnings and inflation data. The Nasdaq eyed its sharpest weekly fall since June 22. Hotter-than-expected consumer and producer inflation reports this week have confirmed that price pressures are extending beyond energy products. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh also said a spending surge was boosting inflation, but added that the US [USN:L6N462084 TEXT:"economy"] remained resilient and benefited from the AI-driven investment boom. Markets increasingly expect the Fed to keep interest rates unchanged this month. Barclays [USN:FWN4622T4 TEXT:"now expects"] 25 basis point hikes each in December and January. Meanwhile, Tesla (TSLA.O) failed to hold on to gains from before the bell — as much as 3% — after unveiling a [USN:L1N46200L TEXT:"redesigned Roadster"], powered by rocket-style thrusters, developed in collaboration with SpaceX. Netflix (NFLX.O) [USN:L4N46128P TEXT:"appointed"] former Disney executive Peter Rice as chief content officer on Thursday. Its shares were down 2.6%. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.04-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by a 1.94-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq. The S&P 500 posted 17 new 52-week highs and no new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 46 new highs and 200 new lows.

item.title: France, Germany strike deal on car emissions and UK special status
item.description: France and Germany struck a deal on Friday to soften proposed EU car emissions rules and open the door for Britain to be treated as a trusted partner under the bloc's Made in EU rules.
item.dc:creator: Philip Blenkinsop
item.content:encoded: France and Germany struck a deal on Friday to soften proposed EU car emissions rules and open the door for Britain to be treated as a trusted partner under the bloc's [USN:L6N45E0Q1 TEXT:""Made in EU" rules"]. The European Commission [USN:L6N3XM0EA TEXT:"proposed last year"] that automakers cut CO2 emissions by 90% from 2021 levels in 2035, with the remaining 10% offset through measures such as the use of low-carbon steel and alternative fuels. Under the Franco-German plan, the 2035 target would be set at 90%, but without the need for additional compensatory measures. The approach is broadly in line with the wishes of German automakers. European automotive stocks gained after the deal was announced, lifting the STOXX 600 Automobile and Parts Index (.SXAP) nearly 2%. The joint plan also addresses an EU proposal introducing local-content and low-carbon requirements for products bought through public procurement, public auctions or subsidy schemes. France has pushed for these products to be limited to those manufactured in the European Union. Other EU members, including Germany, argue that countries closely linked to EU automotive supply chains and free-trade-agreement partners should also be included. The Franco-German plan says that for the automotive sector, "Made in EU" should cover the EU's 27 countries and other European partners that were part of the EU internal market on January 1, 2020. That would include Britain, which left the EU single market at the end of 2020. Volkswagen , Europe's largest automaker, said the compromise would help the industry contribute "to climate protection without jeopardizing its competitiveness." The German company said the "Made in EU" proposals "provide a clear incentive for production and investment in Europe". An official at British Prime Minister Andy Burnham's Downing Street office said inclusion in the "Made in EU" scheme would boost Britain's automotive sector. However, he said the Franco-German proposal requires wider European backing and that details had yet to be seen. The Franco-German plan also says that inclusion should be subject to an agreement on full reciprocity, along with "dynamic alignment with EU conditions for investment from third countries and with EU trade protection measures". That could mean Britain adopting measures the EU has taken to [USN:L6N45V0LF TEXT:"restrict imports"] of Chinese-built hybrid and battery-electric vehicles. Speaking to reporters in London, Renault (RENA.PA) CEO Francois Provost said "obviously, the UK should be part of" the "Made in the EU" scheme as it is part of Europe's automotive "ecosystem." But he said Britain should in turn ditch its [USN:L8N446056 TEXT:"EV sales mandate"] and adopt the same rules as the EU. "The two automotive industrial policies should be consistent," Provost said. A GOOD DAY FOR JOBS OR A 'HISTORIC MISTAKE'? The Franco-German paper also proposed compliance periods spanning multiple years for CO2 emission targets, no revision before 2030 of the utility factor for hybrid vehicles, which measures the share of driving done electrically, and recognition of cars powered by renewable and low-carbon fuels as zero-emission vehicles. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called the deal "a good day for motorists and for jobs in Germany, France and Europe", adding that Italy largely agreed with the proposals. The deal will not please all automakers. Toyota's (7203.T) European division, which sells cars in Europe from plants in the EU, Britain, Turkey and Japan, said on Thursday that including partners such as Britain, Canada, Japan, South Korea and Turkey would give the EU the scale needed to compete with China. [USN:L1N45Z0LF TEXT:"Turkey's trade minister"] said this week on a trip to Brussels that trusted partners like Turkey should not be excluded. Green and environmental groups criticised the emissions proposals. German Greens lawmaker Swantje Michaelsen said Germany's government was holding back the industry as high fuel prices accelerate EV demand. Anna Krajinska of transport and environment campaign group T&E called the deal a "historic mistake" that would reduce the incentive for automakers to invest in EVs. "German and French political leaders claim they are acting to save jobs, but this may well be the deal that buries Europe’s auto industry," she said. France and Germany must convince other EU members and the European Parliament for their plans to enter into force. They are unlikely to reach a final common text before early next year, after an EU-UK summit planned for November 20.

item.title: El cobre impulsa al alza el complejo metalero antes de la LME Week
item.description: Los precios del cobre impulsaron al alza a otros metales básicos el viernes, gracias al apoyo que supuso la debilidad del dólar, mientras que los mercados bursátiles se estabilizaban tras la fuerte caída del jueves en los valores tecnológicos, mejorando el apetito por el riesgo por los metales dependientes del crecimiento.
item.dc:creator: Polina Devitt
item.content:encoded: Los precios del cobre impulsaron al alza a otros metales básicos el viernes, gracias al apoyo que supuso la debilidad del dólar, mientras que los mercados bursátiles se estabilizaban tras la fuerte caída del jueves en los valores tecnológicos, mejorando el apetito por el riesgo por los metales dependientes del crecimiento. * A las 1600 GMT, el contrato de referencia del cobre a tres meses en la Bolsa de Metales de Londres (LME) ganó un 0,3%, a 14.384 dólares por tonelada, recuperándose del mínimo de casi dos semanas de 14.256 dólares alcanzado el jueves. * La reunión anual LME Week, que se celebrará la próxima semana en Londres y a la que acuden consumidores, productores, operadores y corredores del sector de los metales, coincide con el tercer miércoles del mes, fecha en la que vencen los contratos mensuales de la LME. * El cobre y el zinc, junto con el aluminio y el estaño, se encaminan hacia la próxima semana en situación de "backwardation", con los contratos al contado cotizando con una prima respecto a los contratos a tres meses, una estructura que apunta a cierta escasez en la oferta a corto plazo. * "La verdadera escasez de cobre refinado este año se ha debido a que el metal refinado ha seguido inundando el mercado estadounidense ante la perspectiva de los aranceles previstos para enero del año que viene", afirmó Ian Roper, investigador de metales de la correduría Marex, en una presentación. * Sin embargo, Roper prevé que el cobre se vea sometido a presión de cara a fines de año, ya que a principios de diciembre comienza a cerrarse el plazo para que los envíos pasen la aduana estadounidense antes de que termine el año, lo que liberará parte del metal para los mercados fuera de Estados Unidos. * El cobre acumula un alza del 16% en lo que va de año, tras tocar un máximo histórico de 14.875 dólares hace cinco semanas. * Entre otros metales básicos de la LME, el aluminio subió un 0,5%, a 3.001 dólares por tonelada; el zinc ganó un 0,7%, a 3.690,5 dólares; el níquel avanzó un 0,7%, a 15.325 dólares; el plomo mejoró un 0,4%, a 1.887 dólares; y el estaño sumó un 0,3%, a 50.240 dólares.

item.title: Trudy forecast to near Mexico's Pacific coast as major hurricane through the weekend
item.description: Hurricane Trudy rapidly intensified on Friday, carrying maximum winds near 120 mph (195 kph), and is expected to approach Mexico's Pacific coast as a major storm during the weekend.
item.dc:creator: Aida Pelaez-fernandez
item.content:encoded: Hurricane Trudy rapidly intensified on Friday, carrying maximum winds near 120 mph (195 kph), and is expected to approach Mexico's Pacific coast as a major storm during the weekend. Additional strengthening is still forecast before Trudy nears the coast of Jalisco and Colima states late on Saturday as a life-threatening major hurricane, Mexican authorities and the US-based National Hurricane Center warned. It is not expected to make landfall but will remain very close to the coast, about 60 to 65 km away, and any change in its path closer to shore will increase the severity of its impact, the head of Mexico's weather agency Fabian Vazquez said at a press conference. "Everyone in this region needs to be very careful and stay alert over the weekend," he added. Mexico's civil protection agency asked residents to start preparations for the storm's arrival by securing doors and windows, and removing objects that could be thrown around by the strong winds. "Trudy has the potential to even reach Category 4 or 5 intensity," said Alex DaSilva, a hurricane meteorologist at private forecaster AccuWeather. Located about 235 miles (380 km) southwest of resort city Acapulco, the storm is expected to produce up to 15 inches (38 cm) of rain in the states of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco, increasing the risk of life-threatening flooding and landslides, according to the NHC. HARD-HIT PACIFIC COAST The hurricane will strike Mexico's Pacific coast, a region that has already been battered in recent weeks by storms that left several dead and caused severe flooding. "The most critical conditions will start on Saturday, with very severe winds and waves along the coast, in an area that has already been affected for several weeks," Vazquez said. Tropical Storm Simon continues to weaken farther northwest offshore, after [USN:L1N45Y0H6 TEXT:"dropping heavy rain"] along the coast earlier as a hurricane. Last week, tropical storm Rachel hit the Baja California peninsula damaging 1,500 homes, according to Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum.

item.title: Barril sube más de 3% para registrar alza semanal, mercado atento a suministro O.Medio
item.description: Los precios del petróleo subieron más de un 3% para registrar un avance semanal, debido a la continua incertidumbre sobre el suministro en Oriente Medio, mientras los inversionistas seguían evaluando la cantidad de gasóleo que Rusia podría suministrar a los mercados mundiales.
item.dc:creator: Arathy Somasekhar
item.content:encoded: Los precios del petróleo subieron más de un 3% para registrar un avance semanal, debido a la continua incertidumbre sobre el suministro en Oriente Medio, mientras los inversionistas seguían evaluando la cantidad de gasóleo que Rusia podría suministrar a los mercados mundiales. * Los futuros del crudo Brent se disparaban 3 dólares a un máximo de sesión de 109,58 dólares el barril a las 1650 GMT, mientras que los futuros del crudo West Texas Intermediate (WTI) de Estados Unidos sumaban 3 dólares a un pico de jornada de 101,02 dólares y un máximo desde el 21 de septiembre. En lo que va de semana, el Brent ha subido alrededor de un 4% y el WTI un 8,5%. "El conflicto en Oriente Medio sigue reapareciendo y creo que es cuestionable la cantidad de gasóleo que Rusia puede suministrar realmente a los mercados. Esos dos factores siguen impulsando a los operadores a comprar", afirmó Dennis Kissler, vicepresidente sénior de operaciones de BOK Financial. * La inquietud por el suministro también aumentó al recrudecer los ataques en torno al estrecho de Ormuz durante los últimos 10 días, y con Irán afirmando que está intensificando los ataques en respuesta al bloqueo estadounidense de sus puertos y a las sanciones más duras introducidas el mes pasado. * Los hutíes lanzaron el jueves misiles contra el complejo del palacio presidencial de Yemen, en la ciudad sureña de Adén, matando a dos guardias, mientras que la coalición liderada por Arabia Saudita en Yemen detalló decenas de ataques contra infraestructuras saudíes en el marco de este conflicto cada vez más intenso. "La intensificación de los ataques iraníes provocó una fuerte caída de los flujos de crudo del Golfo", dijeron analistas de Kpler en un reporte el jueves, añadiendo que esperan una recuperación más lenta y desigual de los flujos por el estrecho de Ormuz a falta de un acuerdo político global. Mientras tanto, Ucrania atacó el jueves una refinería de petróleo rusa después de que el presidente Volodimir Zelenski declarara que Kiev abandonaba el alto el fuego sobre las instalaciones energéticas anunciado por el presidente Donald Trump y criticara la disposición de este último a llegar a acuerdos con Moscú. La refinería de petróleo rusa de Riazán ha suspendido las operaciones en una unidad de destilación primaria de crudo tras un ataque con drones en la región el jueves, informaron dos fuentes del sector a Reuters. La AIE acordó el jueves liberar más de 20 millones de barriles de combustible al mercado.

item.title: CoreWeave stock, bond set for weekly plunge as rate-hike fears hit AI bet
item.description: CoreWeave's shares and bond were set for steep weekly losses on Friday, underscoring investor worries over the cloud-computing company's $50 billion debt load that has rippled across the AI industry.
item.dc:creator: Shashwat Chauhan, Niket Nishant
item.content:encoded: CoreWeave's (CRWV.O) shares and bond were set for steep weekly losses on Friday, underscoring investor worries over the cloud-computing company's $50 billion debt load that has rippled across the AI industry. The Nvidia-backed company came into focus this week after the latest inflation data boosted bets on [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"interest-rate hikes"], raising the chances of higher payout on borrowings by data center and AI infrastructure firms with huge debt. CoreWeave shares fell more than 11% on Friday, taking their weekly losses to nearly 25%. If the current levels hold, they are set for their worst week in over 11 months. "Its not just CoreWeave, there's several (companies) that are falling into this category because of concerns that the revenue is just not going to be there to turn a profit and maintain the amount of debt that these companies are taking on," said Todd Schoenberger, chief investment officer at CrossCheck Management. Investor worries over CoreWeave's massive debt load had a contagion affect that impacted rival Nebius Group (NBIS.O) , whose shares were set for their steepest weekly fall in two months. Nebius (NBIS.O) dropped 10% and data center operators Applied Digital (APLD.O) and IREN (IREN.O) slipped 9% each. The selloff is a stark reminder that AI companies' reliance on debt is becoming a risk for investors and punctures the notion that companies at the heart of the AI boom are immune to macroeconomic headwinds. CoreWeave's stock has already lost about a fifth of its value, or nearly 9.6 billion, so far this month. The steepest decline this week came on Wednesday, when the stock dropped 15.5%. Short sellers made around $806 million, the fourth best single day for CoreWeave shorts since the stock listed in March 2025, according to data analytics firm ORTEX. DEBT MARKET JITTERS The yield on CoreWeave's October 2031 maturity dollar bond briefly surged past 16% on Thursday. It is set to decline for a fifth straight week, down about 3 cents on the dollar this week. The cost of insuring against CoreWeave's debt has surged past 1,000 basis points to record highs this week, according to data from S&P Global Market Intelligence. Still, several analysts were not ready to throw in the towel. Evercore analysts maintained their outperform rating on CoreWeave stock. "The markets appear to be extrapolating a higher secondary-market bond yield as evidence the business model has stopped working, which we don't think is the case," they wrote in a note. Given the circular nature of AI financing and Nvidia's stake in CoreWeave, Brian Reynolds, chief market strategist at Reynolds Strategy, said Nvidia could also offer buy it. "At a small premium to the current stock price, but far below where the stock had been trading in the past," he said. "We understand that this may not be a likely option, but... it may not be far-fetched." Nvidia is CoreWeave's second-largest investor and its CEO Jensen Huang recently gave the cloud company [USN:L4N46112V TEXT:"a vote of confidence"], saying its financial strength was "improving every day". But his endorsement is yet to lift CoreWeave's stock, a contrast from June when his support for Marvell Technology (MRVL.O) [USN:L4N42A0MP TEXT:"sent shares soaring"]. Other analysts argued the rout in CoreWeave should not be seen as a sign that the AI rally is coming to an end. "You cannot take CoreWeave as the poster child for AI," said Tommaso Leodari, chief investment officer at Dubai-based hedge fund Index & Cie. Exchange traded funds managed by Cathie Wood's ARK Invest have been lapping up CoreWeave shares over the last two sessions, with total purchases exceeding 381,000 shares. Retail investors have also bought into the weakness, buying up net $66 million worth of the stock so far this week, which is the second highest weekly figure on record, according to Vanda data. Separately, regulatory filings showed CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator and entities linked to him have [USN:L6N4620WG TEXT:"sold nearly $1 billion"] of stock, mostly under prearranged trading plans, since the company's IPO in March 2025,

item.title: CoreWeave bond rout tests market's math on AI buildout
item.description: A sharp decline in CoreWeave's bonds this week is emerging as a test of investors' willingness to keep financing the massive buildout of AI infrastructure, as rising borrowing costs and scrutiny of debt-funded expansion hit the sector.
item.dc:creator: Suzanne McGee, Gertrude Chavez-Dreyfuss
item.content:encoded: A sharp decline in CoreWeave's (CRWV.O) bonds this week is emerging as a test of investors' willingness to keep financing the massive buildout of AI infrastructure, as rising borrowing costs and scrutiny of debt-funded expansion hit the sector. Analysts and portfolio managers said the selloff in the data center operator's debt carries more significance than a concurrent rout in its shares because it may signal a broader reassessment of the risks tied to financing AI projects that may take years to generate revenue. CoreWeave bonds issued in June at a yield of 9.675% have plunged in value, sending their yield to 15% this week. "CoreWeave is absolutely the canary in the coal mine" for a market segment that is coming under more stress, said Max Frumes, global head of distressed and leveraged finance at 9fin, a fintech corporate credit data and analytics company. "This is going to be a turning point in the pricing and availability and structure of credit that's supporting the AI boom," said Frumes, who believes that other AI-linked debt will follow CoreWeave into distressed territory. "It's going to get more expensive. There will be a lot more scrutiny and probably some pushback from investors." CoreWeave shares fell 15.1% from Monday's open through Thursday's close, despite a 6% gain on Thursday after a [USN:L4N46112V TEXT:"vote of confidence from partner Nvidia NVDA.O"]. The decline was broadly in line with weakness in other so-called neocloud companies such as Nebius (NBIS.O) and Iren (IREN.O) . Credit investors said they already are [USN:L6N45611M TEXT:"becoming more selective"]. "We're definitely taking another look at our exposures across the AI infrastructure space, particularly where the risks are concentrated and whether we're being adequately compensated for taking them," said John Han, a portfolio manager at fixed-income asset management firm F/m Investments. F/m's portfolio contains unsecured CoreWeave bonds in one of its exchange-traded funds, but only because they make up part of the index tracked by the ETF. At their current yields those bonds "certainly deserve another look," Han said. He generally prefers to invest in high-yield securities via special purpose vehicles that may offer lower yields but also more collateral and less risk. "The market is being very selective and really singling out anything that has more leverage, and (that may be) in a bit more challenging operating environment," said Larry Holzenthaler, senior portfolio manager of fixed income at Catalyst funds. To Holzenthaler and other investors, what the markets are witnessing now is an overreaction as sentiment shifts from being overly upbeat to downright bearish. In June, the risks driving the selloff -- the sheer size of the funding needs, the leverage, the reliance on outside financing, the risk that the GPUs (graphics processing units) being purchased for data centers would be obsolete before the new facilities could open -- were merely overlooked or downplayed. "A few months ago, I would have said people were just too optimistic around AI," Holzenthaler said. Deutsche Bank global head of macro and thematic research Jim Reid sees the market entering a new phase in which debt financing is becoming increasingly important. "As we move to a capex cycle funded out of debt rather than simply free cash flow, we have to increasingly respect the credit price action," Reid wrote in a recent report. "AI financing costs aren't dramatic overall, but there are worrying themes at the edges." Vanguard bond portfolio manager Brad Collins said assessing AI-related debt has become more challenging as issuers bring increasingly large and varied offerings to market, often forcing investors to make decisions in days or even hours. Rising inflation has pushed financing costs higher overall and fueled concern about what lies ahead for mammoth AI capital spending plans. Then there is the [USN:L6N43G12P TEXT:"growing political controversy"] surrounding the construction of data centers. Even one of the tech sector's stalwarts allows that the road ahead may be bumpy at times. Dan Ives, partner and technology analyst at Yorkville Ives, an investment firm, estimates that 5% to 10% of planned projects ultimately will not be built. "The growing noise around data center permitting and midterm rhetoric on power prices has given investors another reason to step back," Ives said.

item.title: UK's FCA lifts bans on four former traders after benchmark-rigging convictions quashed

item.content:encoded: Britain's financial watchdog said on Friday it had revoked bans on four former traders previously sanctioned over the LIBOR and EURIBOR manipulation scandal after the Court of Appeal overturned their convictions earlier this month. The Financial Conduct Authority said it had lifted the bans on Colin Bermingham, Philippe Moryoussef, Jonathan Mathew and Christian Bittar, and had removed the related final notices from its public records.

item.title: China's central bank to further open its financial markets to foreigners, chief says
item.description: China's central bank chief pledged to further open up the country's vast financial markets, saying in a speech that yuan assets can meet global investors' growing need for diversification amid trade uncertainty.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Shen, Selena Li
item.content:encoded: China's central bank chief pledged to further open up the country's vast financial markets, saying in a speech that yuan assets can meet global investors' growing need for diversification amid trade uncertainty. Bank Governor Pan Gongsheng cited rising geopolitical risks, profound changes in the global economic landscape and rapid advances in AI as reasons for China to continue promoting yuan internationalization. "China’s steady economic growth, and rapid development of high-tech industries provide solid support for RMB assets," a People’s Bank of China (PBOC) statement quoted Pan as saying in a Thursday speech given on the sidelines of the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank. The remarks came a day after IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said China [USN:S0N40K04E TEXT:"must pivot"] from export-led growth towards more domestic consumption. In Pan's speech, given to international policymakers at the annual meeting, he also called for Beijing to "shift from exports more toward domestic consumption," according to the statement. TURBULENT MARKETS China has stepped up efforts to open its capital markets, at a time when US President Donald Trump's trade war and unpredictable foreign policies have dented trust in dollar assets. Global financial markets have also become more turbulent as investors increasingly worry about whether companies embarking on massive investment in AI will manage to make sufficient earnings gains amid higher borrowing costs. Pan said the PBOC will promote broader global acceptance and use of yuan bonds as eligible collateral, strengthen cross-border financial infrastructure connectivity and support the development of offshore yuan markets. The bank will continue to expand risk management tools to expedite investment and financing, according to the statement. In a separate speech on Friday, the central bank chief said global economic imbalances "are closely linked to the evolution of the global division of labor, inherent contradictions in the international monetary system, and factors such as chronic high fiscal deficits and high consumption in some countries," according to a separate PBOC statement. "Global imbalances cannot be corrected through exchange rate adjustments," Pan said at the Friday meeting with European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde and Valdis Dombrovskis, the European Commissioner for Economy and Productivity, the statement said.

item.title: European shares close out best week since June as earnings soften blow from tech selloff
item.description: European shares rose on Friday to wrap up their best week since late June, during which strong earnings helped cushion the blow from a global selloff in technology stocks.
item.dc:creator: Avinash P, Niket Nishant
item.content:encoded: European shares rose on Friday to wrap up their best week since late June, during which strong earnings helped cushion the blow from a global selloff in technology stocks. The pan-European STOXX 600 index (.STOXX) rose 0.7% to 644.74 points, touching the highest in over three weeks. The benchmark was up more than 2% for the week. "This week has demonstrated the value of diversification when the concentrated US technology trade comes under pressure," said Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com. A selloff in high-flying tech names on concerns over increased reliance on debt to develop AI infrastructure, alongside worries about competition from China, battered tech stocks this week. However, strong results from computer chip equipment maker ASML (ASML.AS) , chip systems supplier Aixtron (AIXGn.DE) and telecom gear maker Ericsson (ERICb.ST) have helped sentiment. "A very good positive earnings season is really going to boost investor sentiment. It could move markets back up to some of the highs that we've seen recently," said Michael Field, chief equity strategist at Morningstar. Earnings for STOXX 600 companies are expected to rise 20.7% in the third quarter from a year earlier, slightly down from the 21% growth forecast last week, data from LSEG I/B/E/S showed. SAP (SAPG.DE) , ABB (ABBN.S) and Barclays (BARC.L) are some of the firms due to report results next week. Aixtron (AIXGn.DE) advanced 6% after beating order intake estimates for the third quarter and confirming annual guidance. Nordex (NDXG.DE) soared 12.3% after the onshore wind turbine maker posted a better-than-expected third-quarter core profit and lifted its full-year margin forecast. Schneider Electric (SCHN.PA) shares reversed earlier gains and were last down 1.8% after the industrial group raised its 2026 [USN:L6N46209B TEXT:"core profit and revenue"] targets for the second time. The tech sector (.SX8P) was flat while the healthcare sector (.SXDP) eased 0.3% after gaining more than 4.6% over the previous two sessions. Among other movers, Nestle (NESN.S) gained 1.7% after JPMorgan upgraded the Swiss food and drinks group to an "overweight" rating. The gains propped up the food and beverage index (.SX3P) , which rose 1.4%. The euro zone's final HICP inflation reading for September came in at 3.8% year-on-year, in line with economists' expectations but well above the European Central Bank's 2% target, showing price pressures still need to be tamed. The ECB has raised borrowing rates by 50 basis points in 2026 to 2.50%, to curb price pressures stemming from higher oil prices. Investors are already pricing in another quarter-point rate hike at a December meeting, according to data compiled by LSEG.

item.title: UK water regulator finds Severn Trent unit breached wastewater obligations

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: British regulator Ofwat said on Friday that it had found Hafren Dyfrdwy, a unit of Water utility Severn Trent (SVT.L) , in breach of its legal obligations over failures in the management of wastewater and sewage services. The water regulator's investigation found that Hafren Dyfrdwy failed to adequately provide drainage services and manage the contents of its sewer network, breaching its statutory duties Ofwat also found the company had previously breached licence requirements by failing to maintain adequate processes and systems, although it has since put those measures in place The company has proposed an enforcement package worth £280,000 ($372,652), which Ofwat has provisionally agreed to accept The enforcement package will be funded by the company and its shareholders, rather than customers, and must be delivered by 2030 ($1 = 0.7514 pounds)

item.title: Hedge funds' role comes into focus following European bonds turmoil
item.description: A sharp sell-off in European government bonds this month shows how hedge funds' growing role is making a systemically important market more vulnerable — a risk regulators are watching closely.
item.dc:creator: Alun John, Dhara Ranasinghe
item.content:encoded: A sharp sell-off in [USN:L1N45N082 TEXT:"European government bonds"] this month shows how hedge funds' growing role is making a systemically important market more vulnerable — a risk regulators are watching closely. On the surface, the [USN:L1N44U082 TEXT:"reasons for"] a surge in French 10-year yields to 24-year highs were clear: a growing [USN:L8N45U1VY TEXT:"government debt"] burden, inflation fanned by high energy costs, and competition for capital from a global data-centre boom that is lifting economic growth. But some investors said the scale and speed of the moves showed hedge funds were fuelling volatility in the market as they rapidly unwound trades. No obvious trigger preceded the unusually large daily yield increases of over 10 basis points (bps) and nearly 25 bp two-day jump in the premium investors demand to hold French debt over German bonds, the most since the euro zone debt crisis. Yields rise as bond prices fall. , . The European Central Bank estimates that hedge funds account for more than half of trading in the roughly $13 trillion European government bond market, up from 30% in 2020. The International Monetary Fund says hedge fund exposure to sovereign bonds has more than doubled since 2022, without giving a total. "The hedge fund community has ballooned," said Lauréline Renaud-Chatelain, fixed income strategy lead at Pictet Wealth Management. "It's bringing a lot more volatility to the bond market and potentially explains why the (French) sell-off was severe in a context where we lacked a real catalyst." HEDGE FUNDS CAN AMPLIFY PRICE MOVES Hedge funds oversee over $40 trillion, including the borrowed funds they use to leverage their bets and exposure through derivatives, according to the IMF. They rarely share details of their investments and will bet on asset prices falling as well as rising. Their role in sovereign debt trading matters because it impacts governments' funding, which in turn can affect borrowing costs for companies and homeowners. Increased hedge fund trading activity can "amplify price dislocations and liquidity strains during periods of stress," the IMF said in October. It cited hedge funds' borrowing and crowded trades, in which many funds hold similar positions. The European Securities and Markets Authority, the region's financial watchdog, declined to comment for this story. Certain strategies popular with hedge funds are sensitive to price and volatility changes, said Bruno Schneller, managing partner at Erlen Capital Management, which invests in hedge funds. These include cash-futures [USN:L1N45E0NO TEXT:"basis trades"] and leveraged carry trades. In a basis trade, hedge funds seek to profit from the narrow price difference between bond securities and futures. A carry trade involves borrowing cash in a currency with low interest rates to bet on other assets. When things change, "investors may need to reduce exposure relatively quickly ... creating the potential for market moves to become self-reinforcing," said Schneller. But he cautioned against attributing the recent volatility solely to hedge funds given fundamental drivers, notably in France. Political jostling ahead of 2027's presidential election could hinder efforts to reduce France's high deficit, one factor which has rattled markets. HEDGE FUNDS STEP IN AS OTHER INVESTORS DRAW BACK Jiri Krol, global head of government affairs at the Alternative Investment Management Association, a private markets industry group, said hedge funds were one of bond markets' most important sources of liquidity. "As for recent market dynamics, we caution against hasty, broadbrush pronouncements based on anecdotal evidence about the role of particular categories of market participant," he said. Hedge funds have taken a greater share of government bond markets as other buyers retreat. Central banks are shrinking balance sheets, changes in pension schemes are reducing demand for sovereign debt, and regulatory rules mean banks can hold fewer bonds. Their participation can help markets function smoothly in an era of increased government borrowing, while their more frequent trading activity boosts liquidity. "Everyone kind of appreciates the role hedge funds play," said Marion Le Morhedec, Fidelity International's chief investment officer, fixed income. But popular hedge fund trades are crowded and are typically funded by debt, while funds' short-term focus means they can suddenly exit en masse if markets move against them, draining liquidity and exacerbating price moves. Hedge funds "completely wipe out the market in those circumstances," Le Morhedec said. "For me, 100% of the explanation (of early October's low liquidity) is this." Asked about the systemic threat posed by hedge funds, the chief financial officer of Wall Street giant JPMorgan told analysts on Tuesday the industry has been "a source of risk for the system for a long time now, and everyone knows that, including the hedge funds themselves". Their leverage is "in the category of known unknowns," Jeremy Barnum said. "It doesn't mean it's riskless, but we kind of know what it is." ON WATCH In early October, short-dated debt was particularly volatile. France's 2-year bond yield surged, Germany's plunged on safe-haven inflows and the gap between the two widened 21 bps, the most in a day since 2012. Hedge funds often use French government bonds as collateral when borrowing to fund their bets. French debt makes up about €100 billion ($112 billion) of the €250 billion in euro zone government bonds that have been pledged for borrowings in the repo market, Bank of France data shows. The Bank of England is also watching the repo market, a crucial source of funding for financial firms at times of stress. It estimates £85 billion ($113 billion) of the £200 billion net borrowing in gilt repo markets is [USN:L6N45R0WM TEXT:"from hedge funds"]. One big European bond investor told Reuters that hedge funds' role has become a key topic for regulators when they meet with the firm. Pictet's Renaud-Chatelain said liquidity in French bonds in early October had been the worst since 2008. Poor liquidity makes trading harder and brokers charge more. In extremis, they may not provide prices at all, causing markets to seize up. A separate IMF report on Tuesday said markets have [USN:L1N45Z031 TEXT:"managed recent stress well"], however, and the half-dozen fund managers Reuters spoke to said that in general the volatility had not yet affected their strategies, and at times created opportunities. "Volatility sometimes is good ... (French debt) became relatively cheap compared to the credit risk," said Michela Bariletti, chief credit officer at Standard Life. "We look at OATs (French bonds) cautiously but during the sell-off, we actually added a bit." ($1 = 0.8929 euros) ($1 = 0.7543 pounds)

item.title: China's super-rich scramble to exit offshore trusts, raise cash as taxman knocks
item.description: Some of China's richest people are winding down their offshore trusts, selling shares, and even switching nationality as a deadline looms to declare income booked overseas, say wealth advisers, lawyers and others familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Some of China's richest people are winding down their offshore trusts, selling shares, and even switching nationality as a deadline looms to declare income booked overseas, say wealth advisers, lawyers and others familiar with the matter. The move is part of tougher scrutiny of capital outflows and rule enforcement amid growing fiscal strains as the world's second-largest economy battles with persistent weakness in domestic demand and broader economic imbalances. At the same time, tax officials have also stepped up efforts to gather information on wealthy individuals in their jurisdictions and are setting up dedicated teams to scoop up taxes owed on offshore incomes, they said. Founders of Hong Kong- and U.S.-listed Chinese firms would be hit the hardest in the latest tax move, as many of them sold shares through trusts at peak valuations between 2014 and 2020, said Oscar Liu, CEO of wealth adviser JLT Legacy Group. "We estimate that the tax payable in a single case could range from a few million yuan to hundreds of millions, or even billions," said Liu, whose firm has offices in Hong Kong and Singapore. In late July, Beijing set an October 22 deadline for the declaration of offshore trust income, with a tax of 20% to be imposed on such profits, triggering a scramble among wealthy Chinese individuals to tot up liabilities. Boston Consulting Group estimates China's offshore wealth at about $1.7 trillion, and offshore trusts have gained popularity in recent years as a tool for top shareholders of overseas-listed Chinese companies to park wealth outside the country. China's State Taxation Administration has ordered employees to chase up those liable for offshore trust tax, working from a list drawn from the Hurun wealth rankings, corporate filings and other public information, three people said. The people, who have knowledge of the matter, sought anonymity as the measures are confidential. Taxmen in some provinces and cities with numerous wealthy entrepreneurs have set up special task forces dedicated to gathering information on offshore trusts, Liu added. China's State Council, or cabinet, declined to respond to a Reuters request for comment. The State Taxation Administration and the finance ministry did not respond to requests for comments. FINDING CASH The unexpected trust tax move has spurred a dash for cash in some cases. A family office lawyer said clients cannot offset share-price losses against tax bills, while property developers who received large dividends in past years are now too weak financially to pay what they owe, as real estate languishes. A tech billionaire's family office said it now spends more time calculating tax than trading and is selling about half its equity portfolio. "It is like pulling the rug from under one's feet," said a person working there, referring to the demand to pay in cash within three months. Banks are now lending to private clients to cover tax bills, with the loans secured against shares in the clients' own companies, said a private banker with a major international bank who deals with high net worth individuals and family offices. China's offshore trust tax regime has also forced some of its wealthy to restructure businesses and family wealth holdings. Some have even shut newly established trusts before funding them, said one trust lawyer in Hong Kong. A mainlander with Hong Kong citizenship, now working as an insurance agent in the Asian financial hub, said she was giving up her mainland residency to keep her husband's wealth out of Beijing's reach, even though he is not a mainland tax resident. JLT's Liu said few offshore trust holders would rush into new investments, as they calculated tax liabilities. LACK OF CLARITY Even those of China's wealthy who have started looking for options to pay taxes are confused by some aspects of the new rules that are unclear, from coverage targets and retroactive application to payment logistics. "The net is very wide," said Wei Kang, a partner at law firm Charles Russell Speechlys who advises high-net-worth individuals and families on complex trust and estate structures, tax and compliance. July's new tax rule ties liability to whether a taxpayer's "principal economic interest" lies in China, a concept open to interpretation that may not easily be settled by physical presence or citizenship, Kang added. It is also unclear whether tax applies from the time a trust is set up, or for a limited period, she said. The new rules also require those with offshore trust income to submit their own calculation of tax due by the October 22 deadline, and pay once authorities confirm the figure, said JLT Legacy Group's Liu. In practice, however, enforcement varies by city with room in some cases for negotiation on repayment, seven people said. There is also no clear limit on how far back tax liability on dividends or share sales stretches, said three people. "The devil is in the detail," Kang said. "A lot of details are lacking." item.title: Stocks edge lower as dollar heads for weekly loss
item.description: Global stocks edged lower on Friday as markets stabilised after a sharp tech-led selloff, while the dollar headed for a weekly loss.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Howcroft, Chibuike Oguh
item.content:encoded: Global stocks edged lower on Friday as markets stabilised after a sharp tech-led selloff, while the dollar headed for a weekly loss. Markets have been [USN:L1N46113N TEXT:"rattled"] this week by concerns over higher interest rates and the debt-fuelled financing behind the AI boom, triggering a selloff in technology and chip stocks. Traders increased bets on further US rate hikes after [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"stronger-than-expected"] inflation data on Wednesday, while investors piled into Treasuries and other government bonds. On Wall Street, the benchmark S&P 500 and the Nasdaq were trading down and were headed for weekly losses. The Dow was flat but set for a weekly gain. Technology and communication services were driving losses while top gainers were utilities and consumer staples stocks. CoreWeave's (CRWV.O) shares shed 9% on the day and were on track to lose nearly 23% this week amid increasing investor scrutiny of the financing for the massive AI infrastructure buildout. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) rose 0.01%, the S&P 500 (.SPX) fell 0.61%, and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) fell 1.3%. The MSCI World Equity Index lost 0.10% and was set for a weekly loss (.MIWD00000PUS) . European stock indexes, [USN:L1N461090 TEXT:"hit less hard"] by Thursday's selloff, were higher, with the STOXX 600 up 0.67% (.STOXX) . London's FTSE 100 (.FTSE) rose 0.38%. "We're starting to see some cracks in the financing of data centers because you're not too sure who's going to be the winners," Tom Plumb, portfolio manager at Plumb Balanced Fund, said. "Our view is that there's going to be some really significant winners. But you have to be careful on the financing capability because companies don't get into trouble because their assets don't exceed their liabilities. They get into trouble when they have liquidity issues." [USN:L1N462067 TEXT:"Asian stocks"] mostly rose and bond markets steadied on Friday, with investors reversing some of the previous session's moves. Indonesian equities suffered their [USN:L4N46124S TEXT:"biggest drop since 1998"] after index provider MSCI said the country's market no longer merited emerging-market status and outlined plans to remove it from key indexes tracked by funds. DOLLAR FALLS, BONDS RECOVER The dollar index fell 0.23% and was on track for its first weekly decline after four weeks of gains, as lower Treasury yields reduced the currency's appeal. Further worries about AI would push the dollar down further, [USN:L1N46204G TEXT:"analysts said"]. The euro rose from its recent 17-month low. It was last up 0.10% at $1.1232 . The Japanese yen strengthened 0.04% against the greenback to 157.92 per dollar. European government bond yields edged higher, while US bond yields fell. Germany's 10-year yield rose 0.14 basis point to 3.411% . The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes fell 0.17 basis points to 5.085%. Even so, yields have eased this week as investors sought the safety of government debt amid concerns about AI-related companies' finances. G7 government bond markets were on course for their strongest weekly performance since late May. Brent crude futures rose 0.85% to $106.83 a barrel and were headed for a second straight weekly gain amid concerns over Middle East supplies. Attacks around [USN:L1N46201B TEXT:"the Strait of Hormuz"] have surged in the past 10 days. Gold gained support from the weaker dollar, rising 0.17% to about $4,177.14 an ounce.

item.title: Oil prices gain more than 3%, heading for weekly gain with focus on Middle East supply
item.description: Oil prices gained more than 3% and were heading for weekly gains on continued uncertainty over Middle East supplies, and as investors kept assessing how much diesel Russia could supply to the global markets.
item.dc:creator: Arathy Somasekhar
item.content:encoded: Oil prices gained more than 3% and were heading for weekly gains on continued uncertainty over Middle East supplies, and as investors kept assessing how much diesel Russia could supply to the global markets. Brent crude futures were up $3.41, or 3.2%, at $109.34 at 12:41 p.m. ET (1641 GMT), while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures rose $2.74, or 2.8%, to $100.67, crossing $100 for the first time since September 21. So far this week, Brent has risen 4.1% and WTI 8.6%. "Conflict in the Middle East still keeps coming back and I think it's questionable how much diesel fuel Russia can actually deliver to the markets. Those two factors are just continuing to have traders be buyers," said Dennis Kissler, senior vice president of trading at BOK Financial. Supply concerns also increased as attacks around [USN:L1N4600JW TEXT:"the Strait of Hormuz"] surged over the past 10 days, with Iran saying it was stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions introduced last month. Yemen's Houthis also fired missiles at the presidential palace complex in the southern city of Aden on Thursday, killing five people. "Intensified Iranian attacks drove Gulf crude flows sharply lower," Kpler analysts said in a report on Thursday, adding that they expected a slower and more uneven recovery in Hormuz flows in the absence of a comprehensive political deal. Meanwhile, Ukraine struck a Russian oil refinery on Thursday after President Volodymyr Zelenskiy declared that Kyiv was abandoning a ceasefire covering energy sites announced by US President Donald Trump and criticised Trump's willingness to strike deals with Moscow. Russia's Ryazan oil refinery has suspended operations at a primary crude distillation unit following a drone attack in the region on Thursday, two industry sources told Reuters. The IEA [USN:L1N4610MY TEXT:"agreed"] on Thursday to release more than 20 million barrels of fuel to the market. Those margins rose as high as $95 a barrel in September as diesel supply tightened because of the wars in Ukraine and Iran. Brent crude was little changed on Thursday, while WTI settled up more than 3% after news that the US was weighing plans to ease restrictions on the world’s "shadow fleet" of tankers and after a big [USN:L6N46115T TEXT:"US crude stock draw"] on hurricane production shut-ins.

item.title: World's rarest porpoise battles extinction as Mexico shrinks protected area
item.description: Mexico's president said on Thursday a drastic reduction in the protected area for the near-extinct vaquita marina, the world's smallest porpoise, will help fishing communities.
item.dc:creator: Ana Martinez, Sarah Morland
item.content:encoded: Mexico's president said on Thursday a drastic reduction in the protected area for the near-extinct vaquita marina, the world's smallest porpoise, will help fishing communities. Critics say this week's reduction in the area where fishermen cannot use gillnets, long walls of nylon mesh, by 86% to 1,562 square kilometers (603 square miles), about the size of Greater London, threatens the survival of the species. The prior agreement had protected an area similar to the size of the US state of Connecticut. President Claudia Sheinbaum said the new scope aimed to protect biodiversity in the Gulf of California while also allowing fishermen to make a better living. Authorities said the measure took into account proposals by the International Committee for the Recovery of the Vaquita, a government advisory body. Lorenzo Rojas-Bracho, a Mexican marine biologist and leading vaquita expert who took part in the committee, said he hoped a smaller area could concentrate efforts to save the mammal. "It is difficult to enforce a ban over a very large area, which includes vast areas with no recent records of vaquitas," Rojas-Bracho told Reuters. "If you lose a ring you don't search your entire house, you focus on where you lost it." Scientists estimated last year there were just 7 to 10 vaquitas left, including at least one calf. The population has collapsed from around 600 in 1997, largely due to illegal fishing targeting totoaba, whose swim bladders are highly prized in Chinese medicine and can fetch up to $10,000 in Asia. Rojas-Bracho said that if no more vaquitas are killed, the remaining handful of porpoises would have a good chance of repopulating the species. However, he said the area needs more effective tracking of fishing boats, better monitoring and that fishermen should use alternative methods that do not put the vaquita at risk. Gerardo Ceballos, a biologist at the National Autonomous University of Mexico, said allowing the vaquita to become extinct would amount to a moral failure. "What's happening to the vaquita is a death foretold," he said. "We've reduced the vaquita's protected area without actually having the technical or logistical capacity to enforce regulations there; we're giving in to pressure from interested groups so a larger area can be exploited." Ceballos said a very minimal government investment would ensure the vaquita's protection. As things currently stood, however, he believed the porpoise was on the path to extinction. "If the vaquita goes extinct it won't solve insecurity or poverty or any of the local problems. And Mexico would lose an icon," he said. "If actions are taken, there is a possibility, a hope. And we must keep working with hope."

item.title: OFRBS Summary
item.description: L'Europe finit dans le vert, la "tech" pénalise à nouveau le Nasdaq
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'Europe finit dans le vert, la "tech" pénalise à nouveau le Nasdaq 16 octobre (Reuters) - Les Bourses européennes ont terminé en hausse vendredi et sur de solides gains hebdomadaires, les indices du Vieux Continent restant largement épargnés par les craintes sur le secteur technologique qui secouent à nouveau Wall Street, et renouent avec un peu de sérénité grâce à la baisse des rendements obligataires. Shell s’accorde avec DCC Energy sur la cession de ses stations-service en France, selon une source LONDRES, 16 octobre (Reuters) - Shell a scellé une entente avec DCC Energy, basée à Dublin, pour la vente de son réseau de stations-service et de services connexes en France, selon une source proche du dossier et des documents consultés par Reuters. UniCredit autorisé par la BCE à prendre le contrôle de Commerzbank MILAN, 15 octobre (Reuters) - UniCredit a obtenu l'autorisation de la Banque centrale européenne (BCE) pour prendre le contrôle de Commerzbank, a annoncé jeudi soir la banque italienne, alors que son offre publique d'achat hostile a porté sa participation dans son concurrent allemand à 48%. FMI: L'Europe doit stimuler la croissance ou emprunter moins pour garantir la viabilité de sa dette BANGKOK, 16 octobre (Reuters) - L'Europe doit croître plus rapidement ou emprunter moins pour maintenir sa dette sur une trajectoire viable, a déclaré vendredi le Fonds monétaire international (FMI), soulignant que les plans de redressement prévus pourraient ne pas être suffisants. UBS étudie des options à l'étranger au cas la réglementation suisse devient insupportable à ses yeux selon des sources ZURICH, 16 octobre (Reuters) - UBS étudie différents scénarios, dont un déménagement de son siège social ou une fusion avec une autre banque, au cas où la Suisse adopterait de nouvelles règles bancaires que le groupe jugerait excessivement strictes, selon trois sources proches du dossier. Schneider relève ses objectifs 2026 après un T3 record porté par les centres de données 16 octobre (Reuters) - Schneider Electric a relevé vendredi pour la deuxième fois de l’année ses objectifs de résultat d'exploitation et de chiffre d’affaires 2026, porté par la demande des géants du cloud pour les centres de données dédiés à l’intelligence artificielle. Christine Lagarde pourrait être nommée présidente du Forum de Davos dès novembre-sources Le Forum économique mondial (WEF) pourrait nommer Christine Lagarde à sa présidence dès novembre, ont déclaré à Reuters quatre sources proches de l'organisation, ce qui impliquerait un départ anticipé de ses fonctions à la tête de la Banque centrale européenne (BCE). L’AIE va accélérer la mise sur le marché des stocks de pétrole, dont plus de 20 millions de barils de diesel L’Agence internationale de l’énergie (AIE) est convenue jeudi de mettre sur le marché plus de 20 millions de barils de diesel dès que possible, ainsi que les volumes restants des réserves d’urgence libérées en mars, afin de contribuer à approvisionner le marché et à freiner la flambée des prix. États-Unis: Les prix à la production enregistrent en septembre leur plus forte hausse en quatre ans et demi Les prix à la production (PPI) aux États-Unis ont enregistré en septembre leur plus forte hausse en quatre ans et demi, sous l'effet de l'augmentation des coûts des biens et des services, dernier signe en date d'un élargissement des pressions inflationnistes au-delà des produits énergétiques. États-Unis: Les ventes au détail augmentent plus que prévu en septembre avec les prix de l'essence Les ventes au détail aux Etats-Unis ont augmenté plus que prévu en septembre, portées par la hausse des prix de l'essence, même si les dépenses dans d'autres secteurs sont restées modérées, montrent les données publiées jeudi par le département du Commerce.

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'Iran exporte du GPL et du kérosène malgré le blocus américain, selon des données DAMAS/LONDRES, 16 octobre (Reuters) - L’Iran a réussi à exporter quelques cargaisons de gaz de pétrole liquéfié (GPL) et de kérosène depuis juillet, malgré le blocus naval américain, selon des données de suivi du trafic maritime et des sources spécialisées dans la sécurité. Blue Origin vise plusieurs vols de New Glenn par semaine d’ici à 2030 WASHINGTON, 16 octobre (Reuters) - Blue Origin vise plusieurs vols par semaine de sa fusée New Glenn d’ici à la fin de la décennie, a déclaré vendredi un dirigeant de l’entreprise, alors que celle-ci investit des milliards de dollars dans les infrastructures nécessaires pour rivaliser avec SpaceX. Russie et États-Unis discutent de projets dans l'Arctique et dans le GNL, selon un émissaire russe 16 octobre (Reuters) - La Russie et les Etats-Unis discutent de projets dans l'Arctique et dans le gaz naturel liquéfié (GNL), a déclaré vendredi Kirill Dmitriev, l'envoyé spécial du président russe Vladimir Poutine chargé des investissements. USA: Une fusillade dans une école de l'Oregon fait quatre morts, le tireur abattu 15 octobre (Reuters) - Un adolescent de 16 ans a ouvert le feu jeudi dans une école primaire de Bend, dans l'Oregon, faisant quatre morts, dont trois enfants, avant d'être abattu par une personne qui l'avait poursuivi dans l'établissement, a annoncé la police. Attaques de drones russes sur plusieurs villes, dont Kharkiv, au moins trois morts 16 octobre (Reuters) - - Des attaques de drones russes ont fait au moins trois morts vendredi en Ukraine, deux à Kharkiv, la deuxième ville du pays, et un dans la région de Volyn (nord-ouest), ont rapporté les autorités. L'Ukraine dispose de réserves de gaz au plus haut niveau depuis 2020, selon le DG de Naftogaz KYIV, 16 octobre (Reuters) - Le directeur général par intérim de Naftogaz, la société publique ukrainienne du pétrole et du gaz, a dit à Reuters que l'entreprise avait constitué ses plus importantes réserves de gaz depuis six ans en prévision de l'hiver, malgré une recrudescence des frappes russes sur ses installations. Zelensky dénonce la "parodie" diplomatique de Moscou, fustige les expédients de Trump BRUXELLES/KYIV, 16 octobre (Reuters) - Volodimir Zelensky a durci le ton vendredi à l'égard de la Russie, accusée de feindre une "parodie" de processus de paix, et visé par ricochet Donald Trump auquel il reproche de "remplir les poches" de Vladimir Poutine pour poursuivre la guerre en Ukraine. La Chine est prête à coopérer avec l'UE pour remédier aux déséquilibres mondiaux PÉKIN, 16 octobre (Reuters) - La Chine est prête à engager un dialogue avec l'Union européenne (UE) pour améliorer la communication sur certains aspects de la gouvernance économique mondiale et de la coordination des politiques macroéconomiques, a déclaré vendredi le ministre chinois des Finances. La reprise des frappes ukrainiennes contre les raffineries russes est une "honte", dit Trump 16 octobre (Reuters) - La reprise des frappes ukrainiennes contre les raffineries russes est une "honte" qui maintient les prix mondiaux de l'énergie à un niveau élevé, a déclaré le président américain Donald Trump à la chaîne Newsmax lors d'une interview diffusée jeudi. Ukraine : La décision de limiter le réseau Starshield a été prise à la Maison blanche selon des sources NEW YORK/WASHINGTON, 15 octobre (Reuters) - L'ordre de limiter l'utilisation du réseau de satellites à usage militaire Starshield, développé par SpaceX, utilisé par l'Ukraine est venu de la Maison blanche, selon deux responsables américains et un responsable occidental au fait de la question.

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: France et Allemagne d'accord sur un plan pour l'automobile PARIS/BERLIN, 16 octobre (Reuters) - La France et l'Allemagne ont annoncé vendredi un accord sur une "approche commune" visant à garantir l'avenir de l'industrie automobile européenne, avec un accent mis à la fois sur la transition énergétique et sur une production des véhicules en Europe. Les tortues caouannes, sentinelles du réchauffement en Méditerranée PLAGE D'IZTUZU, Turquie, 16 octobre (Reuters) - Sous un ciel baigné de lune, des bébés tortues sortent du sable sur la côte méditerranéenne turque et se hâtent vers la mer, dans un cycle naturel ancestral de plus en plus menacé par le changement climatique. Une étoile verte récemment découverte émerveille les astronomes WASHINGTON, 16 octobre (Reuters) - Pour la première fois, des astronomes ont identifié une étoile verte, un vestige stellaire dense appelé "naine blanche", qui a pris une teinte fantomatique de vert chartreuse après avoir absorbé des débris rocheux provenant de planètes qui, autrefois, gravitaient autour d’elle. La santé du pape Léon en "amélioration constante", dit le Vatican CITÉ DU VATICAN, 16 octobre (Reuters) - Le pape Léon XIV continue de se remettre de son intervention chirurgicale subie mardi pour un nodule cancéreux au poumon, a déclaré vendredi le Vatican, soulignant "l'amélioration constante" de son état de santé. Le pape Léon XIV se rétablit comme prévu de son opération d'un cancer du poumon Le rétablissement du pape Léon XIV de son opération d'un cancer du poumon suit son cours, a annoncé jeudi le Vatican, qui précise que le souverain pontife de 71 ans a recommencé à travailler. Les dirigeants de l'UE se réunissent en sommet, tensions en vue sur le budget Les chefs d'Etat et de gouvernement de l'Union européenne se réunissent jeudi à Bruxelles pour un sommet lors duquel devraient être mises en exergue les divergences sur l'ampleur du prochain budget pluriannuel et sur les priorités de dépense du bloc communautaire, sans accord attendu dans l'immédiat. Macron va effectuer une tournée dans le Golfe, sécurité et énergie au menu Emmanuel Macron effectuera en début de semaine prochaine une tournée dans le Golfe afin de "poursuivre sa mobilisation" auprès de dirigeants régionaux pour revenir à la stabilité et à la libre circulation dans le détroit d'Ormuz, voie cruciale pour les livraisons énergétiques mondiales, a dit mercredi l'Elysée. Albanie: Le Premier ministre exclut de démissionner face aux manifestations étudiantes Le Premier ministre albanais Edi Rama a exclu de démissionner jeudi auprès de Reuters, alors que le pays est secoué par des manifestations étudiantes émaillées de violences. Mélenchon présente un programme budgétaire censé réduire la dette de 25 milliards d'euros Le candidat de La France insoumise (LFI) à l'élection présidentielle, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, a présenté mercredi une feuille de route budgétaire prévoyant plus de 106 milliards d'euros de recettes, 82 milliards de dépenses et une réduction de la dette publique de 25 milliards. Albanie: Manifestations étudiantes, incendie au ministère de l'Education Un incendie s'est déclaré mercredi au sein du ministère albanais de l'Education, à Tirana, en marge de manifestations étudiantes émaillées de violences et de heurts avec les forces de l'ordre, qui ont fait usage de gaz lacrymogène et de canons à eau pour disperser les manifestants.
